subevent.description: After the call ended, Sun Yuwei immediately opened a reading app on her phone, searched for “The Index Fund Investment Guide,” and browsed its introduction, table of contents, and reader reviews. She initially confirmed that the book was suitable for beginners and planned to go to her usual Mingyuan Bookstore the next day to buy the paperback. She then briefly noted her cousin’s key advice on regular investing in her journal, including the frequency, amount, and fund selection method.

name: Fund automatic investment deduction, bookkeeping, and budget check.
description: On December 15, Sun Yuwei's automatic fund investment account automatically deducted 500 yuan to buy a CSI 300 index fund. She opened the mobile bookkeeping app, recorded the investment, and reviewed this month's budget, confirming that progress toward her savings goal of 1500 yuan was going well; her financial discipline was beginning to show results.

subevent.name: Automatic deduction for regular fund investment
subevent.description: On the morning of December 15, 2025, Sun Yuwei's regular fund investment account (linked to her savings card) automatically deducted 500 yuan at the preset time to purchase the CSI 300 Index Fund. She then received a bank SMS notification on her phone confirming that the deduction was successful.

subevent.name: Use the bookkeeping app to record investment expenses.
subevent.description: After receiving the debit notification, Sun Yuwei took out her phone around 10 a.m., opened her usual bookkeeping app, Suishouji, switched to the Investment Expenses category, added a record of 500 yuan with the note: December CSI 300 Index Fund regular investment, and saved it.

subevent.name: Check this month's budget and progress toward savings goals
subevent.description: After recording the investment expense, Sun Yuwei switched to the 'Budget' page in her bookkeeping app and checked item by item whether this month's budgets (dining, shopping, entertainment, etc.) were over budget. She then browsed the 'Savings Goal' module and confirmed that 500 yuan of the 1,500-yuan monthly savings goal had been completed; the remaining 1,000 yuan was planned to be covered by future part-time writing income and daily surplus. She felt satisfied with her financial self-discipline.

name: Develop a habit of daily tea tasting
description: Starting March 24, Sun Yuwei began brewing tea in the morning and evening, replacing the pearl milk tea she used to drink. She incorporated tea tasting into her daily morning yoga practice and nighttime reading, making a tea-tasting journal to record the aroma, flavor, and body sensation of each tea, and her pace of life became calmer.

subevent.name: Design a tea-tasting journal and develop a tea menu.
subevent.description: In her home study, Sun Yuwei took out her journal and designed a tea-tasting record page template, including columns for date, tea name, aroma, taste, and bodily sensation, and planned the order of teas to sample over the coming weeks, incorporating daily tea tasting into her morning yoga practice and nighttime reading plan.

subevent.name: First week of tea tasting practice and journal keeping
subevent.description: Starting from March 24, Sun Yuwei brewed tea at home every morning and evening. After her morning yoga, she would savor a cup of light green tea; while reading in the evening, she would savor a cup of mellow black tea. She recorded in detail the aroma, taste, and physical sensations of each tea in her journal, gradually replacing her usual pearl milk tea. Her daily pace became calmer.

subevent.name: Tea-tasting practice and journaling in the first half of the week.
subevent.description: From March 24 to 26, after doing yoga on the balcony of her home in Kunming each morning, Sun Yuwei brewed a cup of light green tea and quietly savored its aroma and sweet aftertaste; in the evening, while reading in her study, she brewed a cup of mellow black tea and enjoyed the richness and warmth of the tea. After each tea session, she would record in her journal the tea type, brewing temperature, changes in taste, and her current physical sensations and emotions in detail. These three days of practice gradually reduced her dependence on bubble tea, and her pace of life became calmer.

subevent.name: Tea tasting practice and journal recording in the latter half of the week
subevent.description: From March 27 to 30, Sun Yuwei continued the daily rhythm of the earlier part of the week: every morning after yoga she brewed green tea, every evening while reading she brewed black tea, and she recorded her tea-tasting experiences in her journal. As she became more familiar with the character of the teas, she began trying to adjust the brewing water temperature and steeping time to compare the flavor differences caused by different parameters. On the evening of Sunday the 30th, she deliberately reviewed all of the week's records and concluded that she preferred the fresh, clean taste of lightly roasted green tea and the longan-like sweetness of Lapsang Souchong, and she expanded her journal into a complete tea-tasting special topic.

subevent.name: Week 2: Tea tasting practice and journal entries
subevent.description: Sun Yuwei continued to brew tea every morning and evening. This week, she tried a newly unsealed Pu'er tea, savoring its aged aroma and sweet aftertaste. She kept recording her tea-tasting notes in her journal, and further solidified the ritual of tea drinking along with morning yoga practice and nighttime reading.

subevent.name: Beginning the second week of tea tasting practice
subevent.description: After getting up in the morning, Sun Yuwei first did 15 minutes of morning yoga on her balcony, then returned to the tea table in the living room and brewed her daily ripe pu-erh tea, savoring its mellow and smooth texture, and recorded the day's tea-tasting thoughts and physical sensations in her journal. Before bed at night, she brewed another small pot of tea, paired it with reading an essay collection, making tea part of her bedtime relaxation ritual, and added nighttime tea notes to her journal.

subevent.name: Trying freshly opened Pu'er tea.
subevent.description: In the free time of the afternoon, Sun Yuwei decided to open a 2019 ancient-tree raw Pu'er tea cake she had stored earlier. Using a tea pick, she carefully pried off an appropriate amount of leaves, brewed them in a gaiwan, and took time to smell its aged aroma, observe the changing color of the liquor, and savor the slight astringency at first that quickly turned into a sweet aftertaste. As she tasted, she recorded in her journal the new tea's aroma, flavor, and body sensation in detail, compared it with the daily ripe Pu'er, and also photographed the wet leaves to paste into the journal.

subevent.name: Daily tea tasting and journal recording.
subevent.description: Sun Yuwei made tea according to her newly established morning ritual: after getting up, she first stretched for 10 minutes, then brewed today's jasmine tea in a glass cup (she occasionally switches things up), savoring the fusion of floral aroma and tea flavor. She recorded the number of infusions and taste changes in her journal, and drew a simple sketch of the tea leaves unfurling. When reading in the evening, she re-brewed the morning tea leaves and combined her tea-tasting experience with reflections from reading The Book of Tea, writing a long journal entry.

subevent.name: Deep Experience of Pu'er Tea's Sweet Aftertaste
subevent.description: After her morning yoga, Sun Yuwei brewed the raw Pu'er tea she had opened yesterday again. This time she extended the steeping time for each infusion, focusing on how long the sweet aftertaste lingered after the tea liquor went down her throat. She found the tea more mellow than the day before, and the aroma had also developed a honeyed fragrance. In her journal, she used a table to record the liquor color, aroma, taste, and infused leaf state of each infusion, and wrote a preliminary assessment of the tea's aging potential. Before bed, she brewed the late infusions of this Pu'er tea once more and savored its clean sweetness.

subevent.name: Deepen tea-tasting ritual on the weekend.
subevent.description: Because it was the weekend, Sun Yuwei had more time. After breakfast, she deliberately brewed raw Pu-erh tea in a purple clay pot and had it with tea snacks (flower cakes) to experience how the snacks and tea complemented each other. She recorded the entire morning tea-making process in detail, including weighing the tea leaves, controlling water temperature, and the timing of pouring out the tea. In the afternoon, she reviewed the week's tea-drinking diary and made a one-page weekly tea summary in her journal, listing the teas she had tried, her favorite brewing method, and the changes in how her body felt. In the evening after yoga, she drank only plain water so as not to affect her sleep.

subevent.name: Third-week tea tasting practice and journal recording
subevent.description: Sun Yuwei continued to brew and savor tea daily, added white tea tasting this week, compared the physical sensations of different teas in her journal, and began trying to pair light music with tea brewing to further create a tranquil atmosphere. Her tea-drinking habit has become stably integrated into daily life.

subevent.name: Brewing green tea and journaling.
subevent.description: After waking in the early morning, Sun Yuwei went to the quiet study at home, took out the Longjing green tea she had often drunk over the past two weeks, brewed it in a glass cup, watched the leaves unfold, and savored the fresh, sweet aftertaste. She then took out her portable journal, used colored pens to record the taste, aroma, and bodily sensation of the tea, and wrote a short reflection, continuing her established tea-drinking habit.

subevent.name: First tasting of white tea and journal comparison
subevent.description: Sun Yuwei took out a newly purchased cake of aged Shoumei white tea from Fuding, brewed it in a white porcelain gaiwan, and carefully savored the white tea's mellow, jujube-like sweetness and aroma. As she sipped, she sketched the shape of the tea leaves in her journal and wrote a long sensory note, comparing in detail the differences between white tea and the green tea and black tea of the previous two days in flavor, liquor color, and body sensation.

subevent.name: Pairing white tea with light music.
subevent.description: During her evening tea time, Sun Yuwei turned on her phone and played modern piano light music from her collection, and brewed the leftover Shoumei white tea from yesterday in the soothing melody. She listened to the music while tasting the tea, feeling the calm brought by the interweaving of music and tea fragrance. She set aside a special page in her journal to describe the influence of music on the tea-tasting atmosphere and her inner feelings.

subevent.name: Tasting White Peony tea and brewing tea with music
subevent.description: Sun Yuwei switched to another white tea, White Peony, with connected buds and leaves and a fresh, downy aroma. She continued using the same soft music and the same background track for a side-by-side comparison. In her journal she recorded the differences between White Peony and Shou Mei, and tried writing a short essay of random thoughts while tasting the tea.

subevent.name: Weekend deep tea tasting and weekly summary
subevent.description: On Saturday morning, Sun Yuwei deliberately extended her tea-brewing time, chose White Peony, and paired it with different light music (guqin pieces) to explore a more perfect pairing. In her journal, she made a comparison table of the four teas she drank that week (Longjing, Dianhong, Shoumei, and White Peony), summarized the characteristics of each tea, her personal preferences, and changes in physical sensation, and recorded that ‘white tea paired with light music’ had become a new relaxation ritual.

subevent.name: Weekend oolong tea wrap-up and next week's planning
subevent.description: On Sunday evening, Sun Yuwei brewed a cup of light Taiwanese high-mountain oolong tea as the concluding practice of the week's tea tasting. While brewing, she wrote down her overall reflections for the week at the end of her journal, planned to try dark tea or yellow tea next week, and listed new tea samples and journal stickers she needed to buy. The tea tasting ritual came to a successful end in a tranquil atmosphere.

subevent.name: Week 4: Tea Tasting Practice and Journaling.
subevent.description: Sun Yuwei continued her daily morning and evening tea tasting plan. This week she began trying new methods of blended brewing and cold brewing. Her journal entries became richer, including observations on water temperature and brewing time. Tea tasting has become an indispensable daily ritual.

subevent.name: Monday routine tea tasting and journaling
subevent.description: Following the daily plan of tasting tea in the morning and evening, I brewed the tea kept at home with the usual hot-brewing method. I tasted one cup each in the morning and evening, carefully observing the color and aroma of the tea liquor, and recorded in the journal the water temperature of each infusion (about 85°C), the brewing time (30 seconds for the first infusion, increasing thereafter), the tea leaves’ unfolding state, and my own taste impressions. While recording, I also made simple sketches of the tea leaf shapes and wrote a short comment in the margin, such as “crisp and sweet, with a hint of floral aroma.” The whole process took place at the living room tea table at home in Kunming and lasted about 45 minutes.

subevent.name: Tuesday routine tea tasting and journal recording
subevent.description: Continued the morning and evening tea ritual, brewing the same tea leaves as yesterday but adjusting the water-pouring method (changed from high pour to low pour), to observe how the water flow affected the flavor of the tea. In the journal, I added a new column, 'Water-Pouring Method Comparison,' and recorded in detail the differences in the body of the tea under the two methods. After the evening tea, I also spent 15 minutes reviewing the records from the previous two days and added notes in the margins about water temperature changes. The location was still the living room of my home in Kunming, and the whole session took about 50 minutes.

subevent.name: Wednesday routine tea tasting and journaling.
subevent.description: After getting up in the morning, I first sipped a cup of light tea to awaken the body. During a break between study sessions in the morning, I brewed a cup of green tea in a glass, watched the 'tea dance' of the leaves slowly unfolding in the water, and took photos. In the journal, I not only recorded the tea-tasting time and the tea variety (Yunnan green tea), but also used colored pens to draw a diagram of the leaves moving in the water. Before bed at night, I drank a cup of mild black tea. At the end of the journal page, I recorded the day's overall mood and weather conditions, blending tea tasting with feelings from life.

subevent.name: On Thursday, try blending a tea infusion and tasting it
subevent.description: Following this week's plan, she tried a blended brewing method: she put a small amount of Dianhong black tea and dried osmanthus flowers into a gaiwan, quickly rinsed the tea with 90°C water, and then tasted three infusions. For each infusion, she recorded the layered aroma of the tea liquor (osmanthus blossom in the front, black tea base on the finish), the initial sweetness, and the length of the sweet aftertaste. In her journal, she drew a mixing ratio diagram (Dianhong : osmanthus = 3:1) and noted the changes in brewing order. This new experiment excited Sun Yuwei, and at the end of her tea-tasting diary she wrote the note: 'Inspiration: maybe try combining with different floral materials.' The whole process was completed at her tea table at home in Kunming and took about 1 hour.

subevent.name: Try cold-brew tea on Friday
subevent.description: Because the afternoon temperature rose, Sun Yuwei decided to try the cold-brew method. She took 5 grams of the newly bought jasmine tea, put it in a cold-water pitcher, poured in 500ml of purified water, and refrigerated it. She started making it at 3 p.m. and set the cold-brew time to 4 hours. At 7 p.m. she took it out and, while tasting it, noted the cold-brewed tea's clear sweetness and cooling sensation, comparing it with hot-brewed tea. In her journal, she recorded the cold-brew time, tea-to-water ratio, and refrigerator temperature setting, and pasted the label cut from the tea bag as decoration. At the same time, she drew a small refrigerator icon at the bottom of the page to indicate that this was a 'fridge experiment.' The location was the kitchen and living room of her home in Kunming.

subevent.name: Saturday routine tea tasting and journaling
subevent.description: On the weekend morning, Sun Yuwei slept half an hour longer than usual. After getting up, she brewed a cup of ripe Pu'er tea as morning tea. Since she had plenty of time, she deliberately used a purple clay teapot to brew it, experiencing the mellow richness of the tea liquor. In her journal, besides the usual water temperature and brewing time, she added comparison notes between “brewing with a purple clay teapot and brewing with a gaiwan,” concluding that the purple clay teapot is better at retaining heat and releasing aroma. In the evening, she chose a lighter white tea and sketched in her journal the gradual change of the tea liquor to a pale gold color. In total, she spent about one hour on tea tasting and journaling throughout the day, all at her home in Kunming.

subevent.name: Sunday tea tasting and weekly journal summary and plan
subevent.description: On the final day of the week, Sun Yuwei reviewed and organized all the tea-tasting journal entries from the preceding six days. She categorized each day's records as 'regular/mixed/cold brew', used fluorescent stickers to mark new methods worth keeping, and summarized her favorite blended brew of the week (Dianhong + osmanthus). At the same time, at the end of the weekly journal, she planned next week's tea-tasting theme: trying a comparison of different water qualities (such as mineral water vs. purified water). She also wrote an extra 200-character reflection describing how tea tasting helped her slow down and focus on the present. The entire summary was completed at her desk at home in Kunming, and she printed out a group photo of this week's teas and pasted it into the journal.

subevent.name: Week 5 tea tasting practice and journaling.
subevent.description: Sun Yuwei completed the fifth week of building her tea-tasting habit, insisting on brewing tea every morning and evening. On the last day, she organized her journal by stages, reviewed her feelings about the different tea varieties this week, and confirmed that she had successfully replaced milk tea with tea, making her life rhythm calmer and more orderly.

subevent.name: Tasting tea in the morning and evening of the first day
subevent.description: After getting up at 6:30 in the morning, Sun Yuwei went to the kitchen to boil water, took out a can of Yunnan ancient-tree pu-erh tea from the tea cabinet, and brewed it in a purple clay teapot. She poured the tea into a white porcelain cup, sat at her desk, and sipped slowly while savoring the aroma, experiencing the tea's mellow body and sweet aftertaste. At 21:00 in the evening, she brewed tea again, this time choosing Moonlight White, cold-brewing it in a glass, and drinking it while reading essays under the bedside lamp, noting the tea's clarity and coolness.

subevent.name: The next day, savored tea in the morning and evening.
subevent.description: At 8:00 in the morning, Sun Yuwei brewed a pot of Yunnan golden needle black tea in a gaiwan. The tea aroma was rich. As she sipped, she leafed through her journal and wrote down the day's weather and mood. At 15:00 in the afternoon, during the break after the morning class, she held the evening tea tasting early. She brewed a cup of jasmine tea, paired it with a flower cake, and rested on a rattan chair on the balcony, savoring the blend of floral and tea aromas.

subevent.name: Morning and evening tea tasting on the third day.
subevent.description: At 7:00 in the morning, Sun Yuwei tried an aged raw pu'er from Bingdao, brewed carefully with a gongfu tea set, savoring its wild mountain character. At 20:30 in the evening, she switched to ripe pu'er, drinking it in her study while listening to light music, sketching the color changes of the tea liquor in her journal and recording how her body responded differently to raw and ripe tea.

subevent.name: Day 4: tea tasting in the morning and evening.
subevent.description: At 6:45 in the morning, Sun Yuwei brewed a cup of Jingmai Mountain ancient-tree sun-dried black tea. The tea liquor was sweet and smooth, and she paired it with the purple sweet potato cake her mother had made. At 22:00, she brewed a pot of aged white tea and sipped it quietly in the bedroom while flipping through an essay collection. The habit of replacing milk with tea had fully become part of her life, and she felt peaceful inside.

subevent.name: Day 5: Tea tasting and journal organization
subevent.description: At 8:00 a.m., Sun Yuwei brewed the last tea of the month—Bangdong ancient-tree spring tea—and savored its freshness and strength. At 10:00 a.m., she spread her tea-tasting journal for the entire month on her desk and reviewed the records from April 21 to 25 page by page, organizing tasting notes, tea-soup photos, and personal reflections for different teas. She wrote a summary: she had successfully freed herself from dependence on milk tea, her life rhythm had become calmer and more orderly, and she made a simple plan for future tea tasting. The organizing process took about two hours.

name: Older sister Sun Yutong returned to Kunming for a family visit and reunion.
description: On August 22, her elder sister Sun Yutong flew back from Shenzhen to Kunming for annual leave, and their parents prepared a lavish family dinner. From the 22nd to the 26th, the sisters went shopping together, tasted local food, visited Mingyuan Bookstore and Green Lake. Yuwei introduced her sister to yoga and meditation, and also shared the progress of her essay collection and the flower sticker collaboration. Her sister encouraged her to try new things and gave her some advice on promoting a cultural and creative brand. On the evening of the 26th, her sister flew back to Shenzhen. This reunion made the family atmosphere warmer and injected new emotional material into Yuwei's creative work.

subevent.name: Airport pickup and family dinner.
subevent.description: In the morning, Sun Yuwei and her father Sun Mingyuan drove to Kunming Changshui Airport to pick up her sister Sun Yutong, who had flown back from Shenzhen on annual leave. When they got home at noon, her mother Li Xiulan had already prepared a lavish family meal. The family sat around the table together, enjoyed lunch, chatted about recent life, and the atmosphere was warm.

subevent.name: Sisters going shopping, tasting food, and browsing bookstores
subevent.description: In the afternoon, Sun Yuwei accompanied her elder sister Sun Yutong to Nanping Pedestrian Street in downtown Kunming for shopping, tasted local specialties such as flower cakes and mushroom snacks, then walked to Mingyuan Bookstore on Wenlin Street, bought several essay collections and cultural creative products, and briefly exchanged recent reading insights with the bookstore owner Qin Mingyuan.
subevent.location: Kunming - Nanping Pedestrian Street / Mingyuan Bookstore

subevent.name: Visiting Cuihu Lake and doing yoga meditation.
subevent.description: In the morning, the two sisters went for a walk in Cuihu Park, enjoying the lake view and recalling childhood memories. In the afternoon, Sun Yuwei took her sister to Jingxin Yoga Life Studio to try a yoga and meditation class. Her sister became interested in yoga, and after class the two rested briefly at a nearby café.
subevent.location: Kunming - Cuihu Park / Jingxin Yoga Life Center

subevent.name: Sharing creative work and receiving feedback.
subevent.description: At home in the study, Sun Yuwei gave her older sister a detailed update on her ongoing essay collection writing progress and her recent project designing stickers in collaboration with a flower brand. Her sister Sun Yutong, from a product manager's perspective, carefully analyzed the project, offered suggestions on promoting a cultural and creative brand, encouraged her to try more new-media publicity, and promised to help connect her with some resources in Shenzhen.

subevent.name: See my sister off on her way back
subevent.description: In the evening, Sun Yuwei, along with her parents, saw her older sister Sun Yutong off at Kunming Changshui Airport. Her sister was flying back to Shenzhen, and the family said a reluctant farewell. In the departure hall, her sister urged Yuwei to take care of herself and keep writing, and the sisters agreed to meet again next Spring Festival. This reunion infused Yuwei's creative work with new emotional material.

name: Open a stock account and set up a recurring fund investment plan.
description: On November 5, Aunt Xie accompanied Sun Yuwei to a securities company to open a stock account. On November 15, she used a mobile app to set up a monthly automatic deduction of 500 yuan from her writing-income account to regularly invest in the CSI 300 Index Fund, officially starting long-term savings and investment.

subevent.name: Prepare the materials needed for opening an account
subevent.description: After talking with her neighbor Auntie Xie, Sun Yuwei decided to go to the securities company with Auntie Xie to open an account. She prepared her ID card and bank card in advance, put them in her backpack, and agreed to meet Auntie Xie at the entrance of the residential community at nine the next morning.

subevent.name: Go to the securities company to open a stock account.
subevent.description: Accompanied by Aunt Xie, Sun Yuwei went to the Guotai Junan Securities branch in Wuhua District, Kunming. At the counter, she filled in an account-opening application form, completed a risk assessment, and set a trading password, successfully opening a stock account. Aunt Xie offered some advice from the side. The whole process took about two hours.
subevent.location: Wuhua District, Kunming - Guotai Junan Securities Business Department

subevent.name: Set up a regular fund investment plan through a mobile app.
subevent.description: At home, Sun Yuwei logged into the stock account app on her phone and found the automatic fund investment feature. She chose the CSI 300 Index Fund, set up a monthly automatic deduction of 500 yuan from the bank card linked to her royalty payments, and confirmed the settings. After completing it, she took a screenshot for records and noted it in her journal.
subevent.location: Wuhua District, Kunming - home study room

name: Watched Southern Afternoon alone.
description: On the evening of December 23, Sun Yuwei went alone to an art cinema in Wuhua District to watch an art film about the changes in rural Yunnan, *Southern Afternoon*. The film's delicate narrative and imagery reminded her of her own travel and material-gathering experiences. After the screening, she wrote her reflections in the guestbook in the cinema corridor. She decided to incorporate the film's imagery of light and shadow into her next writing.

subevent.name: Decided to watch the movie and checked showtimes.
subevent.description: On the afternoon of December 23, Sun Yuwei, in the study of her home in Wuhua District, Kunming, browsed on her phone the showtimes of an independent art cinema in Wuhua District. She found that the literary film Southern Afternoon was screening that evening; the film tells of changes in the Yunnan countryside. Because of her experiences traveling and doing fieldwork, she was very interested, and immediately bought a ticket online, choosing a seat for the evening show.
subevent.location: Wuhua District, Kunming - home study room

subevent.name: Going to the art cinema
subevent.description: At 6:30 p.m., Sun Yuwei set out on foot from home, walked along Renmin Middle Road toward Green Lake, and arrived at the Elephant Screening Art Cinema on Wenlin Street, Wuhua District, about 20 minutes later. On the way, she wore earphones listening to the film's original soundtrack, feeling calm and expectant.
subevent.location: Daxiang Dianying Art Cinema, Wenlin Street, Wuhua District, Kunming.

subevent.name: Picked up the ticket, entered, and watched the film
subevent.description: Sun Yuwei picked up her ticket at the self-service kiosk in the cinema lobby, then passed through the ticket check to enter Theater 3 and found her seat. The movie started on time at 19:00. She watched "Southern Afternoon" with full attention, moved by the delicate rural light and shadow and the slow narrative pace, recalling her own field trips to Dali, Lijiang, and other places.
subevent.location: Hall 3, Elephant Screening Art Cinema, Wuhua District, Kunming

subevent.name: Write a reflection after the show.
subevent.description: After the movie ended at 21:00, Sun Yuwei walked out of the screening room, paused at the guestbook in the corridor, took out the fountain pen she carried with her, and wrote a reflection of about 200 characters, recording her impressions of the film's light-and-shadow imagery and thinking of the cultural travel essays she was working on.
subevent.location: Corridor of Daxiang Dianying Art Cinema, Wuhua District, Kunming

subevent.name: Return home and organize inspirations
subevent.description: At 21:20, Sun Yuwei left the cinema and walked home, arriving at about 9:40 p.m. She sat at her desk and briefly recorded in her journal the light-and-shadow scenes from the film that had impressed her, and marked imagery she could draw on for her next writing. Then she washed up and rested.
subevent.location: Wuhua District, Kunming - home study room

name: Pottery workshop experience: hand-formed teacups and clay blanks for earrings and pendants
description: On October 30, Sun Yuwei booked a class at an independent pottery studio in Wuhua District, Kunming via WeChat. On the afternoon of November 1, she walked to the studio to learn hand-building techniques. She shaped a clay cup blank for her mother and carved the characters 'Breath' on it, and shaped clay blanks for earrings and a pendant for her elder sister. After class, she took the pieces home to air-dry naturally. The class lasted 3 hours and was her first experience with the feel of clay.

subevent.name: Booking a pottery workshop course
subevent.description: Sun Yuwei contacted an independent pottery studio in Wuhua District, Kunming via WeChat, confirmed a spot in the pottery class on the afternoon of November 1, learned about the course content, fees, and required materials, and completed the reservation.

subevent.name: Heading to the pottery studio
subevent.description: On the afternoon of November 1, Sun Yuwei walked from home to the independent pottery studio near Wenlin Street, Wuhua District, Kunming. The walk took about 15 minutes and she arrived on time.
subevent.location: Kunming - Wuhua District - near Wenlin Street

subevent.name: Learning hand-building techniques.
subevent.description: At the pottery workshop, Sun Yuwei, under the teacher's guidance, learned the basic techniques of hand-building, including wedging clay, rolling coils, and pinching and shaping, familiarizing herself with the feel of clay and modeling techniques in preparation for subsequent work.
subevent.location: Kunming City - Wuhua District - an independent pottery studio

subevent.name: Molded a clay teacup for her mother.
subevent.description: Sun Yuwei used the newly learned hand-pinching technique to shape a clay teacup blank for her mother, paying attention to uniform wall thickness and a round rim. After finishing, she set the blank aside to dry.
subevent.location: Kunming City - Wuhua District - an independent pottery studio

subevent.name: Shaping clay blanks for earring studs and pendant charms for her older sister
subevent.description: Sun Yuwei then shaped a pair of earring-pendant clay blanks for her older sister. Using small tools, she finely carved simple streamlined shapes and, once finished, carefully placed them on a sponge board.
subevent.location: Kunming City - Wuhua District - an independent pottery studio

subevent.name: Engrave words on the bottom of the cup and complete the course
subevent.description: Sun Yuwei used a carving knife to carve the two characters "Breath" into the bottom of the teacup she had made, as a wish for her mother. She then took a photo with the work, cleaned the tools, thanked the teacher, and the class ended.
subevent.location: Kunming City - Wuhua District - an independent pottery studio

subevent.name: After class, tidy up and return home
subevent.description: Sun Yuwei carefully wrapped the three clay pieces, walked back home, placed them in a cool, ventilated area to air-dry naturally, and recorded her reflections on the experience.

name: A warm celebration of the 23rd birthday
description: On July 16, Sun Yuwei celebrated her twenty-third birthday. Her best friends Zhang Jing and Chen Sisi came to her home specially to set up balloons and brought a handmade cake. In the afternoon, the three of them flipped through her college journal albums together. In the evening, her parents cooked longevity noodles, and her older sister Sun Yutong sent a hardcover essay anthology as a gift from Shenzhen. She wrote in her diary: “A year wrapped in love, walking more firmly toward what my heart desires.”

subevent.name: Birthday decoration and celebration with friends.
subevent.description: On the morning of July 16, her best friends Zhang Jing and Chen Sisi came to Sun Yuwei's home at 123 Renmin Middle Road, Wuhua District, Kunming. Together they decorated with balloons and ribbons, and presented a handmade cake and birthday wishes.
subevent.location: 123 Renmin Middle Road, Wuhua District, Kunming, Yunnan Province - Home living room

subevent.name: In the afternoon, flipping through journal and photo albums
subevent.description: In the afternoon, Sun Yuwei and her best friends Zhang Jing and Chen Sisi sat in the bedroom flipping through the journals and photo albums they had made together in college, reminiscing about amusing episodes from their college life.
subevent.location: Home bedroom, No. 123 Renmin Middle Road, Wuhua District, Kunming City, Yunnan Province

subevent.name: Family celebration dinner
subevent.description: In the evening, Sun Yuwei's father Sun Mingyuan and mother Li Xiulan cooked long-life noodles for her, and the whole family sat together to enjoy the birthday dinner.
subevent.location: No. 123 Renmin Middle Road, Wuhua District, Kunming, Yunnan Province - Home Restaurant

subevent.name: Unwrapping sister's gift and writing in diary
subevent.description: Sun Yuwei unwrapped the deluxe prose anthology gift sent from Shenzhen by her older sister Sun Yutong, and wrote birthday reflections in her diary: "A year wrapped in love, stepping more firmly toward where my heart is set."
subevent.location: Home study, 123 Renmin Middle Road, Wuhua District, Kunming, Yunnan Province.

name: Book and shoot a Republic of China-style family portrait
description: On October 2, Sun Yuwei called the "Time Memory" photo studio by Green Lake to book a Republican-era style family portrait for October 3, and informed her parents. On the morning of October 3, the whole family went to the studio, dressed in Republican-era student uniforms and long gowns, and took a warm family portrait. Her mother smiled throughout. After the shoot, they selected photos together and decided to enlarge and frame one group photo.

subevent.name: Making an appointment with the photo studio and discussing the photo shoot details.
subevent.description: On the morning of October 2, Sun Yuwei, at home in Kunming, called "Time Memory" Photo Studio by Cuihu Lake to book a family portrait shoot for the morning of October 3. She confirmed the shooting time, the Republican-era costume sets, and the specific price with customer service, and provided the sizes for her father Sun Mingyuan's dark long gown and her mother Li Xiulan's student uniform. After the call, she sent the booking information and notes to her parents in the WeChat family group, reminding everyone of tomorrow morning's meeting time and dress code.

subevent.name: Going to the photo studio for makeup and costume change
subevent.description: At 8 a.m. on October 3, Sun Yuwei and her parents set out from home and walked to the 'Time Memory' photo studio next to Cuihu Park. After arriving, the family of three was helped by makeup artists in the dressing room to change into Republic of China-style outfits: Sun Yuwei wore a blue student cheongsam and a twin-braid wig, Li Xiulan wore a matching student outfit with light makeup, and Sun Mingyuan wore a gray long gown and round-frame sunglasses. The family was full of laughter throughout, and her mother Li Xiulan was especially happy, taking selfies with her phone from time to time.
subevent.location: Kunming City - Cuihu Photo Studio Dressing Room

subevent.name: Formal family photo shoot
subevent.description: At 9:30 a.m. on October 3, in the Republic of China–style real-scene studio at the photo studio, the photographer guided Sun Yuwei's family of three into warm and natural poses. The background featured an old gramophone, rattan chairs, and a rickshaw prop. They took several sets of photos: a formal group shot of the three sitting side by side, an intimate photo of Sun Yuwei holding her mother's arm, and a family portrait with her father Sun Mingyuan standing behind them. During the shoot, her mother Li Xiulan could not stop smiling, and the photographer captured many natural smiles. The session lasted about 40 minutes and produced about 50 negatives.
subevent.location: Kunming - Cuihu Photo Studio, Republic of China period set

subevent.name: Select photos and determine the fine retouching plan
subevent.description: After the photo session, the family of three browsed the proofs on a computer in the studio's selection room. Sun Yuwei and her parents chose 15 photos they were satisfied with and decided to enlarge and frame a group photo of the three of them sitting on rattan chairs (40 inches). The studio staff recorded the numbers of the selected photos and promised to complete the fine retouching and enlargement within 7 working days and notify them when the photos were ready for pickup. Her mother, Li Xiulan, was very pleased with the results and on the spot ordered two extra 6-inch prints to give to relatives.
subevent.location: Kunming - Cuihu Photo Studio, Photo Selection Room

name: Discussed and completed the publication plan for the essay collection with editor Xu Mingyuan.
description: From November 24 to December 1, Sun Yuwei first organized the manuscript for her essay collection Between Breaths at home and sorted out ideas for the cover design and tagline. Then, on November 26, she reached a preliminary consensus with editor Xu Mingyuan through a WeChat call, and proceeded to write the first draft of the cover design plan and tagline. Finally, on December 1, she worked with the editor to confirm the materials for the topic selection meeting.

subevent.name: Organizing the manuscript for the essay collection Between Breaths
subevent.description: Sun Yuwei organized the complete manuscript of the essay collection "Between Breaths" in her home study, sorted out cover design ideas and initial promotional copy concepts, and prepared for a phone call with editor Xu Mingyuan.

subevent.name: Discuss publishing plans with editor Xu Mingyuan via WeChat call.
subevent.description: Sun Yuwei communicated with editor Xu Mingyuan at home over a WeChat voice call. The two reached a preliminary consensus on the cover design direction, promotional wording, and expected publication date of the essay collection “Between Breaths.” Xu Mingyuan said he would formally submit it to the topic selection meeting in December.
subevent.location: At home in Wuhua District, Kunming City.

subevent.name: Write a cover design plan and draft promotional copy.
subevent.description: Based on her consensus with Xu Mingyuan, Sun Yuwei drafted the cover design plan and promotional copy for the essay collection "Between Breaths" on her computer at home, then sent it to Xu Mingyuan by email for review.

subevent.name: Confirm materials submitted for the topic selection meeting.
subevent.description: After receiving email feedback from Xu Mingyuan, Sun Yuwei made final tweaks to the design plan and promotional copy, and worked with Xu Mingyuan to complete the materials for the topic selection meeting, confirming that all documents were in order.
subevent.location: At home in Wuhua District, Kunming City.

name: Mother's birthday: together with my sister, we gave a massage chair and handmade dried flower bouquets
description: To celebrate her mother's birthday on November 10, Sun Yuwei discussed a joint-purchase plan with her older sister on November 3, selected and ordered a full-body massage chair on November 5, made a dried flower bouquet by hand on November 8, and delivered the gifts to her mother's home on the birthday itself. Her mother was moved to tears, and the scene was warm and touching.

subevent.name: Discussion with sister about co-purchasing a massage chair
subevent.description: Sun Yuwei discussed choosing a birthday gift for her mother Li Xiulan via WeChat with her sister Sun Yutong, who was far away in Shenzhen. The two decided to jointly buy a full-body massage chair, agreeing that Sun Yuwei would be responsible for selecting and ordering it, and her sister would share the cost.

subevent.name: Selecting and ordering a full-body massage chair
subevent.description: In her home study, Sun Yuwei compared several full-body massage chairs on e-commerce platforms, finally chose a model, placed the order and paid the full amount, then notified her sister Sun Yutong to transfer half of the cost.
subevent.location: Wuhua District, Kunming - home study room

subevent.name: Making dried flower bouquets by hand
subevent.description: Sun Yuwei went to Kunming Dounan Flower Market to select dried flower materials. After returning home, she designed and handcrafted a beautiful dried flower bouquet in the living room as one of the birthday gifts for her mother.

subevent.name: Giving a gift on the birthday
subevent.description: It was her mother Li Xiulan’s birthday. Sun Yuwei brought the full-body massage chair she had bought in advance (already delivered) and a handmade dried-flower bouquet to her mother’s home at No. 123 Renmin Middle Road, Wuhua District, Kunming, and gave the gifts to her. Seeing the massage chair and the bouquet, her mother was deeply moved and burst into tears; the scene was warm. Sun Yuwei then video-called her elder sister Sun Yutong so she could join the celebration, and the three shared a birthday cake together.
subevent.location: Wuhua District, Kunming City - mother's home

name: Phone screen accidentally shattered
description: On the evening of December 12, Sun Yuwei walked home from Mingyuan Bookstore. On the bluestone-paved Wenlin Street in Wuhua District, Kunming, she took out her phone to check messages when the strap of her shoulder bag suddenly slipped, causing the phone to fall from her hand. She immediately picked it up and found the outer screen cracked in the upper-left corner, but the touch and display functions were still normal. She gave a wry smile and used the cracked screen to take a photo of the light and shadows where it fell, as a memento.

subevent.name: Phone screen accidentally shattered
subevent.description: On the evening of December 12, Sun Yuwei was walking home from Mingyuan Bookstore. On the bluestone-paved Wenlin Street in Wuhua District, Kunming, when she took out her phone to check messages, the shoulder bag strap suddenly slipped off, causing the phone to fall out of her hand. She immediately picked up the phone and found the outer screen at the upper left corner cracked, but touch and display functions were normal. She used the cracked screen to take a photo of the light and shadows at the spot where it fell as a memento.

name: Keep up the running habit and publish the essay "Pace"
description: After finishing the race, Sun Yuwei kept running three times a week and incorporated what she saw and felt while running into her writing, using the rhythm of breathing during exercise as a metaphor for the rhythm of prose. She later published an essay titled ‘Pace’ in the ‘Kunming Slices’ column, depicting the city’s morning light as seen through a runner’s eyes, which resonated with many fellow runners.

subevent.name: Maintain the habit of running three times a week
subevent.description: Since October 20, 2025, Sun Yuwei has kept the habit of running three times a week, usually in the early morning along Green Lake Park in Kunming or beside the Panlong River, feeling the city's morning light through the rhythm of her breathing while accumulating material for her prose writing.
subevent.location: Kunming City - Cuihu Park and the banks of the Panlong River

subevent.name: Initial two-week running adaptation period
subevent.description: Starting October 20, 2025, Sun Yuwei began a three-times-a-week running plan. On the first day, October 20, she jogged 3 kilometers along the track in Green Lake Park at 6:30 a.m., taking in the morning light and the reflections on the lake. She then ran on October 22, 24, 27, 29, and 31, gradually getting used to the rhythm. Each run lasted about 30 minutes. After finishing, she rested on a park bench and recorded what she had seen and thought that day, building up details for her essays.

subevent.name: Early November running consolidation period
subevent.description: Entering November, Sun Yuwei's running habit gradually became established. She went out at 6:30 every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday morning. This week, her route extended along the Panlong River, running from the riverside path to Dongfeng Square and back, about 4 kilometers in total. During her runs, she focused on her breathing and the changing scenery, observing the colors of Kunming's autumn and winter trees and the morning exercisers. After returning home, she wrote these details into her journal. During this period, she felt her stamina improve and felt better mentally after running.
subevent.location: Kunming City - Along the Panlong River

subevent.name: Late-November running improvement phase
subevent.description: From November 17 to 28, Sun Yuwei ran three times a week, alternating between Green Lake Park and the banks of the Panlong River. She ran once each morning on the 17th, 19th, 21st, 24th, 26th, and 28th. Each run increased to 4.5 kilometers, with a pace stable at around six and a half minutes per kilometer. She began listening to modern pop music while running and composing prose paragraphs in her head, recording her inspirations as voice memos on her phone. During this period, the weather in Kunming turned cooler, so she wore a light sports jacket and still insisted on setting out at 6:30 every morning.
subevent.location: Kunming City - Cuihu Park and the banks of the Panlong River

subevent.name: Stable running period in early December
subevent.description: At the beginning of December, Sun Yuwei's running habit had fully become part of her daily life. On December 1, 3, 5, 8, 10, and 12, she left home at 6:30 a.m. and returned after running 5 kilometers. She found that running not only improved her physical fitness but also made her writing thoughts clearer. During this period, she once met Auntie Xie, a neighbor who was doing morning exercise, at Green Lake Park, and the two briefly chatted about recent updates. She also tried doing simple stretches before running to avoid muscle strain.

subevent.name: Late December: running sprint and summary period
subevent.description: From December 15 to 31, Sun Yuwei continued her running frequency of three times a week, running once on the 15th, 17th, 19th, 22nd, 24th, 26th, 29th, and 31st. She kept the route fixed at Green Lake Park. Because the year was coming to an end, she used her running time to review the year’s writing gains and growth, and conceived the framework of her essay collection in her mind. The run on the morning of the 31st was her last run of the year. She deliberately ran to the vicinity of the Mid-Lake Pavilion, took a sunrise photo as a memento, and decided to carry the running habit into the next year.

subevent.name: Publish the essay 'Pace' in the column.
subevent.description: Sun Yuwei submitted her completed essay "Pace" to the "Kunming Slices" column of "Cultural Vision" magazine. After review by editor Xu Mingyuan, it was published online on December 20, 2025, and the article resonated with many runners.

name: Prepare the annual thesis proposal.
description: On the afternoon of December 15, Sun Yuwei discussed the topic for her annual thesis with her advisor Wu Mingyuan, and settled on the regional writing of contemporary Yunnan prose as the direction. That evening, she organized the discussion notes and made a reading plan. On the morning of the 16th, she went to the library and borrowed essay collections and related works by Yu Jian, Lei Pingyang, and other writers recommended by her advisor. On the 17th, she spent the whole day at home in Kunming writing the first draft of her opening report, planning to polish and submit it before the winter break.

subevent.name: Discussed the topic for the academic year paper with her advisor
subevent.description: On the afternoon of December 15, Sun Yuwei arrived at the office of Professor Wu Mingyuan in the School of Literature at Yunnan University at the agreed time and told her advisor about her research interest in regional writing in contemporary Yunnan prose. Professor Wu fully affirmed the value of the topic and suggested that she focus on reading works by writers such as Yu Jian and Lei Pingyang, and immediately recommended five core references. The two exchanged preliminary ideas on the research framework and agreed to submit the thesis proposal before the winter vacation.
subevent.location: Professor Wu's Office, School of Literature, Yunnan University, Kunming, Yunnan Province

subevent.name: Organize the discussion notes
subevent.description: On the evening of December 15, after returning home, Sun Yuwei organized the afternoon discussion with Professor Wu into electronic notes, including topic directions, key writers, and a reference list, and marked the materials to be consulted next, then made a reading plan for the following week.
subevent.location: Home study, Wuhua District, Kunming, Yunnan Province.

subevent.name: Borrowed recommended books.
subevent.description: On the morning of December 16, Sun Yuwei went to the Yunnan University library, used the library catalog system to search for and borrow five essay collections and related research works recommended by Professor Wu, including Yu Jian's "This Side of Yunnan" and Lei Pingyang's "The Order of Yunnan Dusk," to gather material for her thesis proposal.
subevent.location: Yunnan University Library, Kunming, Yunnan Province

subevent.name: Started writing the thesis proposal.
subevent.description: Throughout December 17, Sun Yuwei, at her home in Kunming, based on her advisor's suggestions and borrowed literature, began drafting the opening report for her academic year thesis, focusing on the research status, significance, and preliminary framework of regional writing in contemporary Yunnan prose. She planned to refine and submit it before the winter break.
subevent.location: Home study, Wuhua District, Kunming, Yunnan Province.

name: Stray dog bite and vaccination
description: On the morning of July 1, Sun Yuwei was bitten on the calf by a stray dog while riding a shared bike to Mingyuan Bookstore. She immediately went to the Third People's Hospital of Kunming to have the wound treated and began a one-month rabies vaccination schedule. The first shot was given that day, and the remaining four were completed on July 4, 8, 15, and 29. During this period, leg soreness and a slight fever affected her yoga practice for a while, but she adjusted her meditation time and wrote about the experience in a short essay, "After Being Bitten," recording fear and acceptance. Her close friend He Lu brought her nourishing soup, and she said with emotion, 'When you are vulnerable, you see warmth more clearly.'

subevent.name: Bitten by a stray dog and given emergency treatment
subevent.description: On the morning of July 1, while riding a shared bike to Mingyuan Bookstore, Sun Yuwei was bitten on the calf by a stray dog near Renmin Middle Road in Kunming. She immediately stopped riding and went to the emergency department of Kunming Third People's Hospital. The doctor debrided and disinfected the wound, stopped the bleeding and bandaged it, and prescribed a rabies vaccine. Sun Yuwei received the first dose of the rabies vaccine in the vaccination room, and the doctor informed her of the follow-up vaccination schedule. The entire process took about 2 hours, after which she returned home to recuperate.
subevent.location: Kunming City - Kunming Third People's Hospital

subevent.name: Second rabies vaccination
subevent.description: As instructed by the doctor, Sun Yuwei went alone to the vaccination room of the Third People's Hospital of Kunming on the afternoon of July 4 to complete the second rabies vaccine injection (second dose). After the vaccination, she stayed for 30 minutes of observation and left after no abnormal reactions. After returning home, she rested and recorded how she felt that day.
subevent.location: Kunming City - Kunming Third People's Hospital

subevent.name: Third rabies vaccination.
subevent.description: On the morning of July 8, Sun Yuwei went to the vaccination room of Kunming Third People's Hospital and received her third rabies vaccine injection (the third dose). The vaccination went smoothly. She asked the doctor about the soreness in her legs and was told it was a common reaction, with a suggestion to apply a warm compress. After the injection, she went home to continue resting.
subevent.location: Kunming City - Kunming Third People's Hospital

subevent.name: Fourth rabies vaccination
subevent.description: On the afternoon of July 15, Sun Yuwei arrived on time at the vaccination room of Kunming Third People's Hospital and completed the fourth rabies vaccine injection (the fourth dose). By then, the soreness in her leg had eased significantly, and she talked with the nurse about her recovery. After the injection, she stayed under observation for 30 minutes; everything was normal, and then she returned home.
subevent.location: Kunming City - Kunming Third People's Hospital

subevent.name: Fifth rabies vaccination
subevent.description: On the morning of July 29, Sun Yuwei went to the vaccination room of Kunming Third People's Hospital for the last time and received the fifth rabies vaccine injection (the fifth dose), marking the complete end of her one-month vaccination schedule. The doctor confirmed that she had effective antibody protection and that the wound was healing well. She felt relieved and, after returning home, informed family and friends.
subevent.location: Kunming City - Kunming Third People's Hospital

subevent.name: Adjusted yoga to meditation due to vaccine reaction.
subevent.description: On July 2, because her legs were noticeably sore and she had a slight fever after being vaccinated the day before, Sun Yuwei was unable to do her usual yoga practice. She decided to cancel the planned yoga class and instead did a gentle meditation practice in her bedroom at home to relieve her discomfort and anxiety. She recorded this adjustment in her journal and thought about how to balance her daily exercise with a recovery period.

subevent.name: Her best friend He Lu brought her some nutritious soup.
subevent.description: On the afternoon of July 3, Sun Yuwei’s yoga partner and best friend He Lu learned that she had been bitten by a dog, so she specially brought a pot of homemade nutritious soup from home to visit Sun Yuwei. He Lu chatted with her for over an hour, comforted her to relax, and shared precautions for the recovery period. Sun Yuwei was deeply moved and later wrote in her diary: “In vulnerability, you see warmth more clearly.”

subevent.name: Wrote the essay "After the Bite".
subevent.description: On July 10, Sun Yuwei used her recovery and rest time at home in her study to write a short essay of about 1,500 Chinese characters, “After Being Bitten,” based on her experience of being bitten by a stray dog and receiving vaccinations. In the essay, she recorded in detail the fear at the moment of the incident, the calmness of the handling process, and the care and warmth she felt during the vaccination period, expressing her acceptance of life's fragility and her gratitude for the kindness around her. After completing the first draft, she shared it with a few close friends via WeChat for feedback, and planned to polish it and submit it to “Cultural Vision” magazine later.

name: Preparing for the National Day family portrait photo shoot in Republican-era style
description: On May 10, while traveling in Hangzhou, Sun Yuwei contacted a photo studio in Kunming to book a Republican-era family portrait shoot on the morning of October 3 and paid a deposit. Later, she discussed clothing styles with her sister, added her mother to the group chat to share old photos of their grandparents and gather opinions. In August, she selected and rented or bought clothing online with her sister. On October 2, she made the final confirmation and preparations before the shoot.

subevent.name: Contact the photo studio and pay the deposit
subevent.description: On May 10, while traveling in Hangzhou, Sun Yuwei contacted a retro Republic-of-China-style photo studio in Kunming by phone and WeChat to inquire about family portrait packages and scheduling. She eventually booked a shooting slot for the morning of October 3 and paid the agreed deposit via WeChat, confirming the reservation.

subevent.name: Discussed clothing combinations with her older sister
subevent.description: Sun Yuwei discussed the clothing style for the family portrait with her older sister Sun Yutong, who lives far away in Shenzhen, via WeChat. Her sister shared some Republican-era styling suggestions and online images, and the two initially settled on simple, elegant qipao and Zhongshan suits as the main tone, and agreed to pick them out together later.

subevent.name: Add mother to the group and share old photos.
subevent.description: Sun Yuwei created a family WeChat group named "Family Portrait Plan" and added her mother, Li Xiulan, and her elder sister, Sun Yutong, into the group. In the group, she shared a treasured old photo of her grandparents from the Republic of China period as a reference for the shooting style, and asked her mother and sister for their opinions on clothing and styling.

subevent.name: Pick out and buy outfits for the family portrait
subevent.description: Sun Yuwei and her older sister Sun Yutong video-called and together browsed local Kunming rental shops for Republican-era style clothing and online purchase options. In the end, they decided to rent two qipao dresses and one Zhongshan suit, and ordered a shawl to match a qipao. All the clothing was delivered to the home in Kunming within a week.

subevent.name: Final confirmation and preparation before filming
subevent.description: The day before the shoot, Sun Yuwei called the photo studio to reconfirm the shooting time, address, and precautions for the morning of October 3, and reminded her family to prepare their clothing and makeup. She then checked and organized the outfits and accessories for the family of four (herself, her parents, and her sister), making sure nothing was left out.

name: Cultural excursion to Hangzhou and Shaoxing for creative inspiration
description: On May 7, Sun Yuwei flew to Hangzhou and stayed at a youth hostel by West Lake. On May 8, she cycled around West Lake and visited Xiaoshu Library and Innocent Times Book Bar. On May 9, she met up with her travel companion Fang Qing in person and explored the artsy neighborhoods together. On May 10, she toured the Xiangshan Campus of China Academy of Art, Nanshan Bookstore, and Bai Causeway on her own. On May 11, she took a high-speed train to Shaoxing, gathered material at Lu Xun's Former Residence, and conceived an essay. On May 12, she returned to Kunming, her trip full of material and reflections.

subevent.name: Fly to Hangzhou and check into a youth hostel
subevent.description: Sun Yuwei flew from Kunming Changshui Airport to Hangzhou Xiaoshan Airport, took the subway to Xihu District, checked into a youth hostel by West Lake, put down her luggage, and rested for a while.

subevent.name: Cycling around West Lake and exploring cultural bookstores
subevent.description: In the afternoon, Sun Yuwei rented a shared bicycle and rode along West Lake, enjoying the lake and mountain scenery. She then visited Xiaoshu Library and immersed herself in a reading space lined with books on the walls. Afterwards, she walked to Innocent Age Book Bar, ordered a drink, sat by the window leafing through an essay collection, and jotted down inspirations.
subevent.location: Hangzhou - West Lake cycling path, Xiaoxiao Library, Innocent Age Book Bar

subevent.name: Meeting Fang Qing in person to explore Hangzhou’s artistic neighborhoods.
subevent.description: Sun Yuwei met up with Fang Qing, her travel companion working in Hangzhou, by the West Lake. Fang Qing led her through independent bookstores and handmade coffee shops in the deep alleys of Shihuqiao Road and Zhongshan Middle Road. The two chatted as they walked, exchanged journal stickers, shared recent creative inspiration and travel experiences, and wrote that day's journal entries in a café.
subevent.location: Independent bookstores on Shihuqiao Road and cafés on Zhongshan Middle Road, Hangzhou

subevent.name: Solo visit to other cultural landmarks in Hangzhou.
subevent.description: Sun Yuwei went alone to the Xiangshan Campus of the China Academy of Art, visited the Folk Art Museum, and appreciated the design aesthetics of architecture integrated with nature. In the afternoon, she returned to Xihu District, selected two books about Jiangnan culture at Nanshan Bookstore, then cycled to Bai Causeway and recorded her thoughts in the twilight.
subevent.location: Hangzhou - Xiangshan Campus of China Academy of Art, Nanshan Bookstore, Bai Causeway

subevent.name: Taking the high-speed train to Shaoxing for cultural fieldwork
subevent.description: In the morning, Sun Yuwei took a high-speed train from Hangzhou East Railway Station to Shaoxing North Railway Station, then transferred by bus to Lu Xun's Hometown. She sat quietly in contemplation before Lu Xun's Former Residence, the Hundred-Plant Garden, and the Three-Flavor Study, used her phone to record the sound of black-awning boats gliding across the water and fragments of dialect from local elderly people chatting, and on the spot drafted an outline for the essay From the Hundred-Plant Garden to the Three-Flavor Study: A New Life in her notes app.
subevent.location: Shaoxing - Lu Xun's Hometown Scenic Area

subevent.name: Return trip back to Kunming
subevent.description: In the morning, Sun Yuwei returned from Shaoxing to Hangzhou, took the metro to Xiaoshan Airport, flew back to Kunming Changshui Airport on an afternoon flight, and was picked up by her parents. The trip officially ended.
subevent.location: Hangzhou - Xiaoshan Airport -- Kunming - Changshui Airport

name: Daily creative routine at the fixed desk in Mingyuan Bookstore.
description: On every working day in August, Sun Yuwei went to her regular seat at Mingyuan Bookstore to write, including revising the essay collection based on feedback from the sample copy, writing column articles, and organizing her planner. She and the bookstore owner, Qin Mingyuan, developed an understanding of how to get along, often exchanging ideas about books and creative writing during breaks. Qin Mingyuan recommended several niche books on Yunnan local history to her, which became important references for supplementing the historical materials in her essay collection. This quiet, book-filled work environment allowed her to advance multiple projects efficiently.

subevent.name: Revising the essay collection proof based on feedback
subevent.description: Sun Yuwei focused on revising feedback on the sample copy of her essay collection at Mingyuan Bookstore. On August 3, 2025, she revised the first three chapters; on August 5, she discussed the chapter structure with Qin Mingyuan, the bookstore owner, who recommended Miscellaneous Notes from Central Yunnan for reference; on August 7, she revised chapters four through six; on August 9, she revised the remaining chapters and completed the final draft.

subevent.name: Revise the first three chapters of the essay collection
subevent.description: At her regular seat in Mingyuan Bookstore, Sun Yuwei focused on revising the first three chapters of her essay collection according to the revision plan. Addressing the loose structure pointed out by her advisor Wu Mingyuan and the language conciseness suggested by editor Xu Mingyuan, she reordered paragraphs and cut redundant descriptions, then marked the corresponding places in the sample book after completing the revisions.

subevent.name: Exchanged ideas with Qin Mingyuan on the chapter structure and consulted reference materials.
subevent.description: While resting at Mingyuan Bookstore, Sun Yuwei discussed the structural issues of chapters 4 and 5 of her essay collection with the bookstore owner Qin Mingyuan. Qin Mingyuan suggested adding more interwoven elements of local Yunnan culture and recommended the book Miscellaneous Notes of Central Yunnan for reference. Sun Yuwei then looked through the book in the bookstore and copied down several passages that could be used as material for the essay collection.

subevent.name: Revising Chapters Four to Six of the essay collection.
subevent.description: At her regular workstation at Mingyuan Bookstore, Sun Yuwei, following Qin Mingyuan's suggestions and the material from *Miscellaneous Notes from Central Yunnan* she had consulted, focused on revising chapters four, five, and six of her essay collection, weaving in details of Yunnan's local culture while adjusting transitions and echoes between chapters to make the content more coherent. After the revisions, she checked the annotations on the sample book again.

subevent.name: Revise the remaining chapters and complete the final draft.
subevent.description: Sun Yuwei, at her regular seat in Mingyuan Bookstore, focused on revising the final three chapters and the afterword of her essay collection. In response to her advisor Wu Mingyuan's comment that the ending lacked a sufficient uplift, she polished the text again and unified the language style across the whole book. After completing the revision, she read through the full text once to confirm no changes had been missed, and then backed up the final electronic version.

subevent.name: Write a column article.
subevent.description: At her regular seat in Mingyuan Bookstore, she focused on writing the column article for 'Culture Vision' magazine, on the theme of Yunnan's local bookstore culture. During writing breaks, she discussed the history of independent bookstores in Kunming with Qin Mingyuan, who provided relevant contacts and leads.

subevent.name: Start writing the column article and have initial discussions
subevent.description: Sun Yuwei arrived at Mingyuan Bookstore at 9 a.m., settled into her usual window-side seat, opened her laptop, and began writing a column article for the magazine "Cultural Vision" on the culture of local Yunnan bookstores. At the beginning of the writing session, she first reviewed her earlier research notes and had a brief chat with the bookstore owner, Qin Mingyuan, confirming the use of the seat for the next few days. Qin Mingyuan encouraged her to write more about Kunming's old bookstores and promised to provide more materials later.

subevent.name: In-depth discussion with Qin Mingyuan on gaining networking leads
subevent.description: During a break in writing, Sun Yuwei and bookstore owner Qin Mingyuan sat down in the bookstore's reading and exchange area and had an in-depth discussion about the history of independent bookstores in Kunming. Qin Mingyuan gave a detailed account of the rise and fall of Kunming's independent bookstores from the 1990s to the present, and provided contact information for several veteran bookstore owners as networking leads, including "Bowen Book House" on Dongfeng West Road and "Jiuyu Xuan" by Cuihu Lake. Sun Yuwei carefully noted key information and interview suggestions, adding rich oral history material for the article.

subevent.name: Complete and submit the column article
subevent.description: After several days of focused writing and revision, Sun Yuwei completed the final draft of her column article at her regular seat in Mingyuan Bookstore. She repeatedly polished the wording, checked the details, and incorporated exclusive material she had previously obtained from Qin Mingyuan, giving the article more depth. At four in the afternoon, she emailed the article to the editor, Xu Mingyuan, along with a writing note. Before leaving, she expressed her gratitude to Qin Mingyuan for providing his connections and venue support.

subevent.name: Organizing the journal and cultural exchange
subevent.description: At her regular seat in Mingyuan Bookstore, she organized her travel and daily life journals and recorded her creative insights from the whole of August. She had multiple in-depth exchanges with Qin Mingyuan about Yunnan local history and literary creation. Qin Mingyuan recommended several niche books, providing historical material for her essay collection. At the same time, she completed the last overdue writing task of the month.

subevent.name: Organize the travel journal and first visit Mingyuan Bookstore
subevent.description: In the morning, she went to Mingyuan Bookstore. After sitting down in her regular seat, she took out her travel journal and various ticket stubs and stickers, and began organizing the journal pages from her early August trip to Dali in chronological order. She drew small illustrations of the scenic spots with watercolor pens and pasted in tickets and postcards. After the lunch break, she chatted with the bookstore owner Qin Mingyuan in the reading area about the historical anecdotes of Dali, Yunnan. Qin Mingyuan pulled two books, Stories of the Nanzhao Kingdom and Travel Notes on the Tea Horse Road, from the bookshelf and recommended them to Sun Yuwei as supplementary local history materials for her essay collection. At 5 p.m., she packed up her tools and went home.

subevent.name: Organizing daily life journals and exchanging ideas on literary creation
subevent.description: In the afternoon she came to Mingyuan Bookstore again and organized her daily-life journal since August at her desk, including records of gatherings with friends, notes from flower-arranging class, reading excerpts, and so on. She decorated the pages with stickers and tape and wrote down her creative reflections for the week. In the evening Qin Mingyuan joined in, and the two of them had an in-depth discussion about the language style of modern essays and the current state of Yunnan literature. Qin Mingyuan also recommended the annotated edition of Border Town and the essay collection Yunnan Camellias. Sun Yuwei carefully noted these recommendations, planning to borrow and consult them. She left at seven in the evening.

subevent.name: Complete this month's overdue manuscript tasks and write creative reflections
subevent.description: In the morning, she took her laptop to her fixed workstation at Mingyuan Bookstore and focused on completing the last overdue article of the month—the Kunming Old Streets series essay for Cultural Horizon. It took about three hours to finish the first draft, which she proofread herself and emailed to the editor Xu Mingyuan. Afterward, she used the remaining time to write August creative reflections in her journal, recording the month's sources of inspiration, difficulties encountered, and the historical material insights gained from Qin Mingyuan. At six in the evening, she ended work, bought a newly arrived essay collection at the bookstore, and went home.

subevent.name: Wrapped up and exchanged concluding thoughts with Qin Mingyuan.
subevent.description: In the afternoon, she went to Mingyuan Bookstore for the last time to do a final check and summary of the journals and creative notes she had organized over the past ten-plus days. She put loose papers back in place and added the book list recommended by Qin Mingyuan to the reference pages of her journal. In the evening, she had a wrap-up conversation with Qin Mingyuan in the bookstore's coffee corner. Sun Yuwei shared the creative inspiration she had drawn from these historical books, and Qin Mingyuan praised her and suggested she incorporate elements of local history into her essay collection. The two agreed to exchange new chapters at the beginning of next month. She said goodbye and went home at seven in the evening.

name: Xishuangbanna plant-themed inspiration trip
description: On October 27, Sun Yuwei prepared for her trip at her home in Kunming, packed her luggage, and bought a high-speed rail ticket. From October 28 to 30, she took the high-speed rail to Xishuangbanna, checked in at a Dai-style homestay in Gaozhuang, and carried out a three-day plant-themed field trip. During the trip, she visited the Xishuangbanna Tropical Botanical Garden, Chinese Academy of Sciences, taking many photos of exotic flowers and rare trees; under a bamboo stilt house by the Luosuo River, she wrote the essay 'The Depth of Green'; and she participated in the homestay owner's handmade Dai-paper workshop, pressing plant fibers into the paper. This short trip accumulated first-hand material for her 'Yunnan Nature Writing' series and also reshaped her view of her ability to travel independently.

subevent.name: Pre-trip preparation
subevent.description: At her home in Kunming, Sun Yuwei packed her luggage, checked her camera and notebook and other field collection tools, bought a high-speed rail ticket online from Kunming South Station to Xishuangbanna Station, and confirmed her reservation at the Gaozhuang Dai ethnic homestay.

subevent.name: Took the high-speed rail to Xishuangbanna.
subevent.description: Sun Yuwei took the high-speed train from Kunming South Station to Xishuangbanna Station, a journey of about 3.5 hours. Along the way, she enjoyed the scenery outside the window, used her phone to record inspiration, and planned a route for creative field collection.
subevent.location: Yunnan Province - Kunming South Station to Xishuangbanna Station

subevent.name: Checked into a homestay in Gaozhuang and tried handcrafted Dai paper
subevent.description: After Sun Yuwei arrived in Xishuangbanna, she checked in at a Dai ethnic guesthouse in Gaozhuang Xishuangjing, put down her luggage, and rested for a while. In the evening, she joined a handmade Dai paper craft activity organized by the guesthouse owner. She pressed the plant fibers she had gathered into the pulp and made a sheet of handmade paper with natural texture.
subevent.location: Yunnan Province - Xishuangbanna Dai Autonomous Prefecture - Gaozhuang Dai-style Homestay

subevent.name: Visited the Tropical Botanical Garden of the Chinese Academy of Sciences
subevent.description: After breakfast, Sun Yuwei went to the Xishuangbanna Tropical Botanical Garden, Chinese Academy of Sciences. She spent the whole day deeply exploring the rare flowers and exotic trees area, taking many close-up photos of plants, and recording the forms, colors, and growing environments of various tropical plants to accumulate visual material for nature writing.
subevent.location: Yunnan Province - Xishuangbanna Dai Autonomous Prefecture - Mengla County - CAS Tropical Botanical Garden

subevent.name: Writing the essay 'The Depth of Green' on the banks of the Luosuo River.
subevent.description: After visiting the botanical garden in the afternoon, Sun Yuwei sat down on the bamboo observation deck by the Luosuo River, opened her notebook, and, drawing on the details of the plants she had observed during the day and her inner feelings, completed the first draft of her essay “The Depth of Green” in one go, recording the deep and shallow greens and vitality of the tropical rainforest.
subevent.location: Yunnan Province-Xishuangbanna Dai Autonomous Prefecture-Bamboo House by the Luosuo River

subevent.name: Return to Kunming
subevent.description: Sun Yuwei checked out of the guesthouse in Gaozhuang, took a stroll in the morning, browsed the local market, and bought some Dai handicrafts as souvenirs. In the afternoon, she took a high-speed train from Xishuangbanna back to Kunming, ending this field trip, and returned home to organize her photos and notes.
subevent.location: Yunnan Province - Xishuangbanna Dai Autonomous Prefecture to Kunming City.

name: A brief encounter with Lin Shen during graduation season; hazy feelings became creative inspiration.
description: At dusk on June 10, while sorting supplies for the used-book drifting event at Mingyuan Bookstore, Sun Yuwei ran into Lin Shen, a guy who often came to the bookstore. He offered to help her carry things, and the two hit it off over their shared love of The Little Prince. She learned that Lin Shen was a history graduate student at the same university, about to graduate and leave Kunming. Over the next ten-plus days, they met several times at the bookstore, talking about books and graduation plans, and gradually developed an unspoken rapport. On the evening of June 20, before leaving the school, Lin Shen came to the bookstore to say goodbye and gave her a volume of modern poetry he had copied out by hand. Yuwei watched him leave and later wrote these hazy feelings into her essay 'A Solitary Journey,' which was included in her essay collection 'Slow Travel Notes.' After that, they occasionally interacted on social media but never met again.

subevent.name: Ran into Lin Shen at Mingyuan Bookstore at dusk.
subevent.description: At dusk on June 10, 2025, while Sun Yuwei was organizing supplies for a used-book drifting activity at Mingyuan Bookstore in Kunming, she ran into Lin Shen, a young man who often came to the bookstore. Lin Shen took the initiative to help carry supplies. The two started talking because they both loved The Little Prince, and discovered they were students at the same school—Lin Shen was a history graduate student about to graduate and leave Kunming. They chatted in the bookstore for about an hour about literature and graduation plans. Lin Shen said he often visited this bookstore and would come again.

participant.name: Lin Shen
participant.relation: The boy she met at the bookstore.
