subevent.name: Met and talked with Lin Shen multiple times at the bookstore.
subevent.description: Between June 11 and June 19, Sun Yuwei and Lin Shen repeatedly ran into each other at Mingyuan Bookstore. Every time they met, they talked about recent reading, graduation plans, and how reluctant they were to leave Kunming. A tacit understanding gradually grew between them, and Yuwei felt a faint stirring of affection, but neither of them spoke it out. Lin Shen revealed that he would leave school on June 20, and Yuwei felt a faint melancholy of parting.

participant.name: Lin Shen
participant.relation: The boy she met at the bookstore.

subevent.name: Lin Shen bids farewell and gifts a hand-copied selection of poems
subevent.description: On the evening of June 20, 2025, before leaving school, Lin Shen made a special trip to Mingyuan Bookstore to say goodbye to Sun Yuwei. He gave Yuwei a personally handwritten anthology of modern poetry and said he hoped she would continue writing. Yuwei was deeply moved and watched Lin Shen leave the bookstore and disappear into the night. After this farewell, the two never met again.

participant.name: Lin Shen
participant.relation: The boy she met at the bookstore.

subevent.name: Composed the essay "A Solo Journey" and included it.
subevent.description: Touched by the emotions of meeting and parting with Lin Shen, Sun Yuwei completed the essay "A Solo Journey" in her home study on June 21, transforming her faint inner feelings into words, and included it in her essay collection "Slow Travel Notes."
subevent.location: Home study, Wuhua District, Kunming City

name: Started a flower sticker collaboration with Zhou Lin; the first trial batch sold out in two days
description: On August 9, Sun Yuwei and her close friend Zhou Lin (an illustrator) officially launched the “Kunming Flower Series” sticker collaboration. They chose six flowers, including camellia, blue jacaranda, and magnolia. Zhou Lin drew the line art, and Yuwei wrote the flower-language copy. On August 23, the first trial batch of 300 sticker sets came off the production line. That evening they were listed on WeChat Moments and the “Yuwei Slow Notes” shop, and within 48 hours they were snapped up by old friends and fans, unexpectedly bringing in their first cultural and creative product income.

subevent.name: Collaborative planning and design phase.
subevent.description: On August 9, Sun Yuwei met with her close friend Zhou Lin at a café in Kunming to officially launch the 'Kunming Flower Series' sticker collaboration project. The two discussed and selected six locally representative flowers as themes: camellia, jacaranda, magnolia, cherry blossom, rose, and azalea. Zhou Lin was then responsible for drawing line drafts of each flower, and Sun Yuwei was responsible for writing literary flower-language captions for each. On August 12, Sun Yuwei completed the first draft of the captions and sent it to Zhou Lin for comments; on August 14, Zhou Lin completed the first draft of the line drawings and discussed revision directions with Sun Yuwei over video. The two communicated frequently through WeChat until the final version was finalized on August 19, when Sun Yuwei handed the design to a printing house to arrange trial production.

subevent.name: Kickoff discussion at the café
subevent.description: Sun Yuwei met her best friend Zhou Lin at an independent café in Kunming and officially launched the 'Kunming Flower Series' sticker collaboration project. While sipping brown sugar pearl milk tea, the two discussed flower-themed ideas. After three hours of brainstorming, they settled on six locally representative flowers: camellia, jacaranda, magnolia, cherry blossom, rose, and azalea. Sun Yuwei is responsible for the flower-language copywriting, and Zhou Lin is responsible for the line art, agreeing to each complete their first drafts by August 14, keeping in close contact via WeChat in the meantime.

subevent.name: Write the first draft of the flower-language copy.
subevent.description: At her desk at home, Sun Yuwei wrote a literary flower-language passage of about 200 characters for each of six flowers. She consulted essay collections and books on plant culture and wove meanings such as camellia as 'ideal love,' jacaranda as 'tranquility and far-reaching aspirations,' and magnolia as 'nobility and gratitude' into the text. At 3 p.m., she sent the completed draft to Zhou Lin via WeChat, along with a request for revision suggestions.
subevent.location: Yunnan Province - Kunming City - home study

subevent.name: Draw line draft and have initial communication
subevent.description: Zhou Lin completed the initial line drawings of six flowers at her desk in the Yunnan University dormitory, using a drawing tablet to carefully render the petal and vein details in each image. At eight in the evening, she sent the line drawings to Sun Yuwei via WeChat, and the two had about a two-hour video discussion on flower proportions and the placement of matching text. Sun Yuwei suggested adjusting the direction of the jacaranda branches, and Zhou Lin said she would refine it in the revised draft.
subevent.location: Yunnan Province - Kunming - Yunnan University Dormitory

subevent.name: Finalized and sent to print
subevent.description: After a week of revisions online, Zhou Lin completed the final version of the line drawing, and Sun Yuwei also fine-tuned the wording of the flower language. At ten in the morning, the two confirmed the final design draft on WeChat. Sun Yuwei then took a USB drive to a partner printing factory in Wuhua District, Kunming, where she explained in detail to the production supervisor the size, material, and quantity requirements for the stickers (500 of each design, 3,000 in total), and paid a deposit. The factory promised to complete the proofing by August 28.
subevent.location: Yunnan Province-Kunming-Wuhua District, a printing factory

subevent.name: Trial production and online launch
subevent.description: On August 23, the first batch of 300 sets of the “Kunming Flowers” series stickers completed trial production. Sun Yuwei and Zhou Lin counted and checked the finished products at Sun Yuwei’s home. After confirming that everything was correct, that evening they put them on sale simultaneously through Sun Yuwei’s WeChat Moments and the “Yuwei Slow Record” online mini store, with moderate pricing and a limited-time discount.
subevent.location: Yunnan Province - Kunming City - Sun Yuwei's home

subevent.name: Sold out and revenue recognition
subevent.description: On August 25, about 48 hours after going on sale, the first batch of 300 sticker sets was snapped up by old friends and fans. Sun Yuwei and Zhou Lin reviewed the sales data on the online backend and were surprised to find that the revenue far exceeded expectations. It was Sun Yuwei's first income from cultural and creative products. The two excitedly shared their joy on WeChat and briefly discussed a follow-up restocking plan.

name: Passed the C1 driver's license exam and obtained the driver's license.
description: On October 15, Sun Yuwei passed the Subject 3 road test on her first attempt and successfully obtained a C1 driver's license. She then posted a photo of the license on her Moments with the caption, 'Steering wheel in hand, distance in sight.' On October 17, she had dinner with her parents to celebrate. On October 20, she began planning a short self-driving trip, initially selecting destinations around Kunming. This series of events marked the successful completion of her plan to learn to drive.

subevent.name: Completed the Subject 3 road test and passed on the first attempt.
subevent.description: Sun Yuwei arrived at the driving test center at 8:30 and entered the waiting room to wait for her number to be called. Around 9 o'clock, it was her turn. Under the examiner's instructions, she got into the car, adjusted the seat, rearview mirrors, fastened her seatbelt, and completed other preparations, then took the light simulation test. Next, on the actual test road, she completed starting, moving straight, upshifting and downshifting, changing lanes, making a U-turn, pulling over, and other items. The whole process took about 20 minutes. Her operation was standard and smooth, and she passed the road test on the first attempt.
subevent.location: Kunming - First Driving Test Center Road Test Site

subevent.name: Received C1 driver's license
subevent.description: After passing the road test, Sun Yuwei went to the license issuance hall at the driving test center around 10 a.m., submitted her ID card, student file, and score report, and waited for the license to be made. At about 11 a.m., she successfully received her C1 driver's license. She carefully examined the photo and information on the license, feeling a strong sense of accomplishment and joy.
subevent.location: Kunming City – No. 1 Driving Examination Center, License Processing Hall.

subevent.name: Posted a photo of my driver's license on Moments.
subevent.description: Around 12 noon, Sun Yuwei returned home. At the desk in her bedroom, she took out her newly obtained driver's license, took a photo with her phone, carefully composed the WeChat Moments post 'With the steering wheel in hand, the horizon is in sight,' and published it to her Moments. Soon after, she received likes and congratulatory comments from close friends Zhang Jing, Wang Xinran, Chen Sisi, and roommates Liu Jia and Zhao Xiaowen, among others. She replied to each one with thanks.

subevent.name: Had dinner with family to celebrate.
subevent.description: At 6 p.m., Sun Yuwei had dinner at home with her father Sun Mingyuan and mother Li Xiulan. During the meal, she excitedly recounted the exam process and her joy at getting her driver's license. Her parents were happy for her and reminded her to drive safely in the future. Her mother Li Xiulan specially made her favorite crossing-the-bridge rice noodles and flower cakes to celebrate. The family atmosphere was warm and cheerful.

subevent.name: Started planning a short road trip with a rental car.
subevent.description: The next morning at 10:00, Sun Yuwei opened her laptop in the study and browsed car rental platforms (such as China Auto Rental and eHi Car Services) to compare destinations around Kunming suitable for self-driving trips. She mainly considered Fuxian Lake, Dali Old Town, and other directions, and looked up routes and parking information along the way. She wrote an initial plan in her journal: to rent a car on a weekend at the end of October and invite her best friend Zhang Jing on a two-day short road trip.

name: Planned the "Winter Reading Marathon" with Qin Mingyuan, a 24-hour relay reading event.
description: From the afternoon of November 22 to the afternoon of November 23, Sun Yuwei and bookstore owner Qin Mingyuan jointly held a “Winter Reading Marathon” at Wheat Field Bookstore. Nearly twenty book lovers took turns reading for 24 hours. She served as host and took part in the late-night reading of Calvino's “Invisible Cities”, sparking discussion about the metaphors of memory and the city. Under the warm yellow lights, the scent of books lingered, and it became a warm winter memory.

subevent.name: Event planning and preparation.
subevent.description: Sun Yuwei and Qin Mingyuan, owner of Maitian Bookstore, co-planned the “Winter Reading Marathon” event: on November 14, 2025, they finalized the theme “Memory and the City” and selected reading passages at the bookstore; on November 16, they published a recruitment post online; on November 17, they designed and put up offline posters; on November 19, they purchased supplies and refreshments; on November 20, they set up the venue and debugged equipment; on November 21, they conducted a final pre-event check. Throughout the process, they recruited readers through both online and offline publicity and completed all preparations, including supplies and the venue.

subevent.name: Confirm the event theme and selected reading pieces
subevent.description: Sun Yuwei and Qin Mingyuan, owner of Wheat Field Bookstore, sat face to face in the reading area on the second floor of the bookstore to discuss the specific direction of the 'Winter Reading Marathon' activity. The two exchanged their thoughts on urban memory and finally set 'Memory and the City' as the event theme. Sun Yuwei recommended Calvino's Invisible Cities as the core piece, and Qin Mingyuan added local prose pieces such as Wang Zengqi's Rain in Kunming. Together they selected about ten reading pieces and printed out a list.

subevent.name: Online event recruitment
subevent.description: At home, Sun Yuwei used her laptop to write the event recruitment post, paired with a hand-drawn style promotional poster (which she designed herself and scanned), and published it through the Wheat Field Bookstore's WeChat official account and Weibo account. The post introduced the event theme, time, location, and registration method in detail, and included a registration link. Sun Yuwei then shared the article to her WeChat Moments and several local culture enthusiast group chats, and Qin Mingyuan also promoted it in the bookstore's reader group.

subevent.name: Create and put up offline posters
subevent.description: Qin Mingyuan used the computer at the creative desk in the back of the bookstore to design and print five A3-size color event posters. The posters included the event name, theme, time, and a QR code for registration. Then, together with Sun Yuwei, he posted them in the storefront window at the bookstore entrance, at two nearby independent cafes ("Maan Coffee" and "Bookworm Coffee" on Wenlin Street), and on the bulletin board outside Yunnan University's East Gate, in order to attract more potential readers.

subevent.name: Purchase event supplies and refreshments.
subevent.description: Sun Yuwei and Qin Mingyuan went together to Walmart Supercenter (Wuhua District store) and the nearby Jiahua Bakery to buy supplies for the event. They bought two cases of bottled water, a bag of Yunnan small-grain coffee beans (for fresh grinding), tea bags in three flavors, flower cakes, egg tarts, and disposable cups and plates. Qin Mingyuan also brought a pour-over coffee kettle and two bottles of homemade plum wine from home, while Sun Yuwei brought a bouquet of dried flowers from home as table decoration. All the supplies were moved back to the bookstore that afternoon for temporary storage.

subevent.name: Set up the venue and test the equipment.
subevent.description: Sun Yuwei and Qin Mingyuan made the final venue arrangements and equipment debugging at Wheat Field Bookstore. They slightly adjusted the original bookshelf layout, cleared an open area in the center of the reading section, and placed a dozen folding chairs and cushions to form a semicircular reading area. Qin Mingyuan carried an old CD player and two Bluetooth speakers down from the attic, connected them, adjusted the volume, and played soft background music. Sun Yuwei placed an event booklet and a pen on each chair, set out the purchased flower cakes and egg tarts on two long tables, and put dried flowers in glass vases in the center of the tables. Finally, they checked the lighting and projector to ensure all equipment was working properly.

subevent.name: Final check before the event.
subevent.description: The day before the event, Sun Yuwei went alone to Wheat Field Bookstore and did a final full check with Qin Mingyuan. They went over the event schedule to make sure every reader had received the reminder notice; checked whether the refreshments were sufficient, and rearranged the spacing of tables and chairs. Qin Mingyuan adjusted the sound system and microphone again to ensure there was no static. Sun Yuwei also put up sign-in instruction stickers at the bookstore entrance and placed the sign-in sheet on the counter. The two briefly rehearsed the opening remarks and transition lines, confirmed their roles (Qin Mingyuan hosting the opening, Sun Yuwei keeping time and guiding the tea break), then closed the store and left, confirming that all event supplies were ready.

subevent.name: Event kickoff ceremony
subevent.description: On the afternoon of November 22, the “Winter Reading Marathon” was officially launched at Wheat Field Bookstore. Sun Yuwei opened the event as the host, introduced the rules and procedures, Qin Mingyuan gave a welcome speech, and the first book friend began reading aloud. Nearly twenty book friends sat in a circle, and the atmosphere was warm and cozy under the soft yellow lights.

subevent.name: Relay reading and late-night reading aloud
subevent.description: From the evening of November 22 into the late night, the relay reading continued. During the late-night slot, Sun Yuwei read selected passages from Calvino's 'Invisible Cities' and led the readers present in a discussion of the metaphor of 'memory and the city.' Everyone shared their own impressions and memories of cities, and the interaction was lively.

subevent.name: Morning session: relay reading and discussion
subevent.description: On the morning of November 23, the book club members in the relay continued reading aloud the pieces they had brought, and held an open discussion around the theme “Warm Winter.” Sun Yuwei served as the host to guide the conversation, as everyone shared reading insights and winter memories.

name: Submitting to the Publisher and Gaining the Editor’s Appreciation
description: On October 5, Sun Yuwei organized the manuscript of Slow Travel Notes in her home study and wrote personalized submission letters. On October 8, she selected three local publishers from the publishing progress schedule she had made the previous month and sent them the manuscript along with the submission letters. On October 12, an editor from one of the publishers invited her for a meeting at a café on Wenlin Street. After flipping through the manuscript, the editor praised it: “The manuscript has a spark of life; the writing has a sense of breath.” However, due to the publishing house's topic selection cycle, he suggested formally submitting it at next spring's topic selection meeting. Sun Yuwei gladly accepted and remained composed.

subevent.name: Organizing the manuscript and submission letter
subevent.description: In her study at home in Kunming, Sun Yuwei, following the publishing schedule set last month, pulled up the final manuscript of "Slow Travel Notes" on her computer, carefully proofread it, and printed three bound copies. At the same time, based on the stylistic features of the three local publishers (Spring City Literature and Art Publishing House, Dianchi Book Society, and Yunling Culture), she wrote personalized submission letters that introduced the manuscript's theme and creative background in detail, and attached her brief bio and contact information. After about two hours of organizing and checking to ensure the manuscripts and letters were error-free, she placed the three sets of materials into large envelopes, affixed stamps, and prepared to mail them the next day.
subevent.location: Wuhua District, Kunming - home study room

subevent.name: Send out the manuscript
subevent.description: On the morning of October 8, Sun Yuwei took three kraft paper envelopes containing manuscripts and submission letters and walked to the People's Middle Road Postal Branch in Wuhua District, Kunming, near her home. At the counter, she purchased registered mail service and sent the three letters to the editorial departments of three publishing houses. After mailing them, she recorded the mailing date and tracking number for each publisher in her phone's memo app for future follow-up. The whole process took about 40 minutes. When it was done, she felt relieved and looked forward to feedback from the publishers.
subevent.location: Kunming City, Wuhua District - Renmin Middle Road Post Office

subevent.name: Met with the editor and gained their appreciation.
subevent.description: At 2 p.m. on October 12, Sun Yuwei arrived on time at the “Slow Time Café” on Wenlin Street to meet Zhou Mingyuan, an editor at Yunling Culture Press. Zhou Mingyuan flipped through the printed manuscript and praised, “The manuscript has a lively spirit; the words have a breathing quality.” But he also explained that the publishing house holds topic selection meetings quarterly, and this winter's meeting had already ended, so he suggested formally submitting the manuscript to next spring's topic selection meeting. Sun Yuwei said she fully understood and thanked the editor for his recognition. The two also talked about the conception and writing background of some chapters in the manuscript, and the meeting lasted nearly an hour. Afterward, Sun Yuwei jotted down this pleasant meeting on a small card at the café.
subevent.location: Slow Time Café, Wenlin Street, Wuhua District, Kunming

name: Journal sharing event at the community library.
description: On December 19, Sun Yuwei carefully selected journal works and organized her tools in her study at home in Kunming for the next day's sharing session. On the morning of December 20, she went to Cuncaoxin Community Library in Wuhua District to hold the second free sharing session on 'Life Aesthetics in Journaling'. She showed her travel journals, reading journals, and inspiration collection notebooks, and taught everyone how to record daily life using collage, watercolor, and simple composition. An older woman took her hand and said, 'You remind me of myself when I was young.' She wrote in her journal: 'Sharing makes the beauty of solitude flow.'

subevent.name: Prepare materials and journal pieces for the sharing session
subevent.description: Sun Yuwei, in the study of her home in Wuhua District, Kunming, selected representative pages from her travel journal, reading journal, and inspiration notebooks, and organized collage and watercolor tools and composition examples to prepare materials for the next day's sharing session. She sorted the journals by theme and wrote a brief presentation outline to ensure the sharing content was smooth and clear.
subevent.location: Home study, Wuhua District, Kunming, Yunnan Province.

subevent.name: Go to Cuncaoxin Community Library
subevent.description: On the morning of December 20, Sun Yuwei walked from her home on Renmin Middle Road to the Cuncaoxin Community Library in Wuhua District, carrying her prepared journal works and presentation materials. On the way, she bought a cup of brown sugar pearl milk tea, feeling relaxed and expectant.
subevent.location: Wuhua District, Kunming, Yunnan Province - Renmin Middle Road to Cuncaoxin Community Library.

subevent.name: Hosted a journal-sharing session and interacted.
subevent.description: Sun Yuwei held the second free sharing session, “The Aesthetics of Life in Journaling,” in the reading room of the Cuncaoxin Community Library. She showed about twenty community residents her travel journals, reading journals, and inspiration notebooks, explaining collage, watercolor, and simple composition techniques on site, and led the participants in hands-on practice. An auntie was so moved by her sharing that she took her hand and said, “You remind me of my younger self.”
subevent.location: Reading Room, Cuncaoxin Community Library, Wuhua District, Kunming, Yunnan Province

name: Incorporate watercolor hand drawing into daily creation and sharing.
description: Starting from late October, Sun Yuwei incorporated watercolor hand-painting into her journal diary and travel records. She first bought art supplies, then created a watercolor journal of the Erhai Lake sunset; in November she discussed a "Yunnan Flora" watercolor sticker series collaboration with Zhou Lin; in December she shared beginner painting tips on her WeChat official account, attracting new followers.

subevent.name: Buy watercolor painting materials
subevent.description: To incorporate watercolor hand-painting into her journal and travel records, Sun Yuwei went on the afternoon of October 28, 2025, to a long-established art supply store on Renmin Middle Road, Wuhua District, Kunming. She carefully selected Winsor & Newton watercolor paints, brushes of different sizes, 300g watercolor paper, and a new large journal. After returning to her home study, she spent an hour trying out the new tools, testing pigment spread and brushstroke effects, completing her material preparations before creating.
subevent.location: Art supply store in Wuhua District, Kunming, Yunnan / home study

subevent.name: Paint a watercolor journal spread of the Erhai Lake sunset.
subevent.description: On the morning of November 2, 2025, Sun Yuwei painted a watercolor of the Erhai sunset in her home study, based on her memory of a previous creative field trip to Erhai Lake in Dali and the photos on her phone. She used the wet-on-wet technique to capture the gradient colors of the sky and a dry brush to depict the shimmering light on the lake. After completing the painting, she trimmed it and pasted it onto that day's journal page, writing her reflections on the scenery in the surrounding blank space with a fountain pen. This was the first time she formally incorporated a watercolor painting into her journal diary.

subevent.name: Discussing the "Yunnan Plants and Trees" sticker series with Zhou Lin
subevent.description: On the evening of November 15, 2025, Sun Yuwei discussed the collaboration plan for the next season's 'Yunnan Flora' watercolor sticker series with her college roommate Zhou Lin via a WeChat voice call. The two analyzed one by one the watercolor rendering effects of candidate plants such as Yunnan lilac, notoginseng flower, and Cangshan azalea, and settled on a soft watercolor style for the sticker series, planning to make 10 individual stickers. In addition, they also discussed details such as contacting a printing house, listing on Weidian, and pricing strategy. The entire call lasted about 90 minutes.
subevent.location: Kunming, Yunnan Province - home study (online communication)

subevent.name: First time sharing watercolor insights for complete beginners on a WeChat official account
subevent.description: On the afternoon of December 1, 2025, Sun Yuwei edited and published a WeChat official account article from her study at home in Kunming, titled "A Beginner's Guide to Watercolor Sketching from Scratch: From Erhai Sunset to Journal Creation." The article introduced in detail her self-taught watercolor tool list (recommendations for paints, brushes, and paper), basic techniques (wet-on-wet, dry brush), and how to combine watercolor painting with journal entries. It also included step-by-step creation images of the Erhai sunset work, the final finished piece, and journal layout mockups. Within three hours of publication, it received more than 50 reads and over a dozen comments, and gained 8 new followers, marking an initial attempt at the content transformation of the official account.

name: Attended the recorded basic watercolor course and completed systematic study and organization.
description: On August 15, 2025, Sun Yuwei signed up for an 8-week recorded basic watercolor course. She then bought watercolor materials and set a Wednesday evening study reminder. From August 20 to October 8, she followed the course every Wednesday evening to practice techniques such as wet-on-wet, dry layering, and masking fluid, pasting her practice pieces into her journal and writing reflections on them. On October 10, she organized all her works and journal entries, wrote a learning review, and shared it on social media, completing a systematic course of study.

subevent.name: Registered and prepared watercolor materials
subevent.description: On August 15, Sun Yuwei enrolled in an 8-week recorded basic watercolor course on an online platform, paid the course fee, and obtained the course link. She then went to an art supply store in Wuhua District, Kunming, and bought basic tools such as watercolor paints, watercolor paper, brushes, masking fluid, and a palette, as well as an A5-sized journal for recording study notes and pasting practice works. After returning home, she organized the materials and set a weekly reminder for Wednesday evenings.

subevent.name: Practice Session 1: Wet-on-Wet Basics
subevent.description: At 8 p.m. on Wednesday, August 20, Sun Yuwei opened the first lesson of the watercolor recorded course in her study, learning the basic techniques of the wet-on-wet method (laying water, dropping color, and diffusion effects). Following the video, she sketched with a pencil, then practiced painting a gradient sky and a simple cloud. After finishing, she pasted the work into her journal and noted with a label: "Too much water makes it flow easily; control the amount of water next time." The whole process lasted about 1.5 hours.

subevent.name: Second lesson practice: dry stacking technique
subevent.description: On Wednesday evening, August 27, Sun Yuwei studied the second lesson: the dry layering method. She first layered colors on practice paper with a dry brush, practicing gradients and color mixing, and then painted a strawberry as the themed assignment. After finishing, she took a photo with her phone to keep as a record and wrote down the lesson from her failure in her journal: "I layered before the first coat was completely dry, so the picture turned out muddy." After recording her reflections, she pasted the practice work into the journal.

subevent.name: Third practice session: using masking fluid
subevent.description: On the evening of Wednesday, September 3, Sun Yuwei learned how to use masking fluid properly. She first used masking fluid to draw the outline of leaves and petals, waited for it to dry, then applied the background color, and finally rubbed off the masking fluid. The practice theme was a single leaf, and it came out quite successfully. She wrote down the steps in detail in her journal and pasted in the finished work, with the note: "It must be completely dry, or it won't peel off cleanly."

subevent.name: 4th course exercise: simple representation of flowers
subevent.description: On the evening of Wednesday, September 10, Sun Yuwei learned how to paint a simple little daisy in watercolor. She used wet-on-wet technique for the base color and dry layering for the petals, and also tried the splatter technique to add interest. After finishing the piece, she compared it with her previous practice pieces, felt the progress, and wrote in her journal: "This time the overlapping petals look much more natural."

subevent.name: Course Practice 5: Landscape Sketch Composition
subevent.description: On Wednesday evening, September 17, Sun Yuwei studied the composition and coloring of landscape sketches. The course theme was “Distant Mountains and Lake.” She practiced using the wet-on-wet technique to express the mountain gradients and the lake reflections. After finishing the piece, she was not quite satisfied with the sky transition and wrote in her journal: “Uneven water application caused mottled color patches; use a larger brush next time.”

subevent.name: Sixth course practice: combining watercolor with line drawing
subevent.description: On the evening of Wednesday, September 24, Sun Yuwei learned how to combine line art with watercolor painting using a waterproof technical pen. She first drew the line art of a rose, then applied light watercolor washes. After finishing the piece, she really liked this style. She pasted the work in her journal and wrote: "Line art makes watercolor clearer; I can try this more often in the future."

subevent.name: Course practice session 7: comprehensive technique exercise—flower bouquet.
subevent.description: On Wednesday evening, October 1, Sun Yuwei studied comprehensive watercolor techniques and painted a mixed bouquet using wet-on-wet, dry layering, and masking fluid. She carefully planned the composition and completed a fairly complete piece. She turned her journal to a new page, pasted in the work, and annotated: "Using wet-on-wet for the base and then dry layering for details works best."

subevent.name: 8th course practice: final work—Small Landscape.
subevent.description: On the evening of Wednesday, October 8, Sun Yuwei finished her final class. The course-ending assignment was to freely create a small landscape. She chose a corner of Green Lake in Kunming and, using the techniques learned over the eight weeks—wet-on-wet painting, dry layering, masking fluid, and line drawing combined—she completed a watercolor piece about A5 in size. She pasted the work into her journal and summarized: "Over the eight weeks, I mastered the basic techniques, especially the fluidity of wet-on-wet painting."

subevent.name: Course summary and organizing works.
subevent.description: On October 10, Sun Yuwei organized all the practice works and journal records she had completed during the eight-week course. She protected her favorite pieces with page pockets, decorated the journal and added supplementary annotations, and wrote an about-800-character review of the course, posting it on her personal social media as a commemoration. She also took stock of the remaining watercolor materials and planned the next stage of advanced study.

name: Set up the flower arrangement practice area at the yoga studio and do slanting-style practice every Tuesday and Thursday.
description: On August 31, 2025, Sun Yuwei set up a flower arrangement practice area in a corner of Kunming Jingxin Yoga Life Studio. Starting September 2, she practiced basic ikebana forms alone every Tuesday morning from 7:00-8:00, focusing on reviewing the slanted composition; every Thursday morning from 7:00-8:00 she practiced alone in the same place (except September 11), repeatedly working on securing flower materials, adjusting angles, and trimming branches based on workshop notes, and cleaned up the space after each practice. On the morning of Thursday, September 11, He Lu (yoga instructor) temporarily acted as her student, and Sun Yuwei explained the design concept and fixation techniques of the slanted composition to her, deepening her own understanding through teaching.

subevent.name: Set up the practice area of the yoga studio.
subevent.description: Sun Yuwei set up her ikebana practice area in a corner of Jingxin Yoga Lifestyle Studio in Kunming (on the side near the window). She laid down a waterproof mat and arranged flower containers, scissors, flower materials, and workshop notes, preparing for the upcoming Tuesday and Thursday morning practice sessions.
subevent.location: Kunming City - Jingxin Yoga Life Center

subevent.name: Tuesday morning ikebana practice (slanted style)
subevent.description: Every Tuesday from 7:00 to 8:00 in the morning, Sun Yuwei practices basic flower arrangement forms alone in the practice area of the yoga studio, focusing on reviewing the oblique composition. Referring to her workshop notes, she repeatedly drills fixing flower materials, adjusting angles, and pruning branches and leaves, and cleans up the space after each practice.
subevent.location: Kunming City - Jingxin Yoga Life Center

subevent.name: Thursday morning flower arrangement practice (slanting style)
subevent.description: Every Thursday morning from 7:00 to 8:00, Sun Yuwei practices basic flower arrangement forms alone in the practice area of the yoga studio, focusing on reviewing the slanted composition. She repeatedly practices fixing the flower materials, adjusting angles, and trimming branches and leaves while referencing the workshop notes, and cleans up the space after each practice. Note that September 11 is arranged separately due to He Lu's participation.
subevent.location: Kunming City - Jingxin Yoga Life Center

subevent.name: Thursday morning flower arrangement practice (He Lu as the student)
subevent.description: On Thursday morning from 7:00 to 8:00, Sun Yuwei practiced ikebana in the practice area of the yoga studio. He Lu (yoga instructor) temporarily acted as her student. While demonstrating, Sun Yuwei explained the design concept and fixing techniques of the slanted composition, deepening her understanding through teaching.
subevent.location: Kunming City - Jingxin Yoga Life Center

name: Launch a series of flower arrangement experience classes at the yoga studio.
description: On October 20, yoga instructor He Lu noticed that Sun Yuwei had obtained her ikebana certificate and suggested offering a monthly ikebana experience class. Sun Yuwei designed three progressive lessons: understanding flower materials and fixed compositions, combining main and secondary branches, and creating free-style arrangements. She purchased flower materials on October 24, and the first class was held on the evening of October 25 with 8 participants. The subsequent classes were held on November 22 and December 20, with attendance growing to 10 and enthusiastic feedback. After the course ended, they discussed the plan for the next year.

subevent.name: Proposal and course design
subevent.description: On the afternoon of October 20, yoga instructor He Lu saw the ikebana certificate Sun Yuwei had recently obtained at Kunming Jingxin Yoga Life Studio and suggested offering a monthly ikebana experience class at the studio as a value-added service for members. Sun Yuwei readily agreed and designed a three-session progressive course outline on the spot in the studio's lounge area: Session 1, learning about flower materials and basic fixed forms; Session 2, learning how to pair the main and guest branches; Session 3, completing a free-style ikebana work.
subevent.location: Kunming City - Jingxin Yoga Life Center

subevent.name: Purchasing flower materials for the first class
subevent.description: On the morning of October 24, Sun Yuwei went to the Dounan Flower Market in Kunming to buy materials for her first flower arrangement class—flowers such as roses, eucalyptus leaves, and daisies, along with a kenzan, flower scissors, and practice containers. She also talked with a longtime stall owner at the market about seasonal flower combinations, spending about 200 yuan in total. In the afternoon, she carried the flowers to the Jingxin Yoga Life Center, sorted and trimmed the stems in advance, and arranged the ten practice tables in the classroom.

subevent.name: First ikebana experience class
subevent.description: On the evening of October 25, from 17:30 to 19:30, Sun Yuwei held her first flower arrangement trial class at the Jingxin Yoga Lifestyle Center, with He Lu helping with check-in and distributing tools. Eight yoga members participated. The course included recognizing flower materials, fixing stems on a kenzan, and practicing basic compositions. Sun Yuwei guided the students one by one in trimming branches, and each student completed a small Ohara-ryu style piece. After class, the students responded enthusiastically and all said they looked forward to the follow-up courses.
subevent.location: Kunming City - Jingxin Yoga Life Center

subevent.name: Second flower arrangement experience class
subevent.description: On the evening of November 22, 17:30-19:30, Sun Yuwei attended her second flower arrangement trial class at Jingxin Yoga Life Center. The theme was the matching and spatial composition of the main branch and guest branch. All 8 students from the first class attended, with 2 new members signing up, for a total of 10 people. Sun Yuwei first demonstrated how to fix the main branch and guest branch, then the students practiced while He Lu helped pass out flower materials. After the class, Sun Yuwei organized the students' works and took photos for archiving.
subevent.location: Kunming City - Jingxin Yoga Life Center

subevent.name: Third flower arrangement experience class
subevent.description: On the evening of December 20, 17:30-19:30, Sun Yuwei attended her third ikebana experience class at Jingxin Yoga Lifestyle Center, with the theme of creating free-style flower arrangements. Ten students each completed a free-style flower arrangement independently using what they had learned in the previous two classes. Sun Yuwei reviewed each work in turn and gave suggestions for improvement from three aspects: line, color, and space. After class, He Lu and Sun Yuwei discussed the course plan for the next year in the rest area of the yoga center, and initially decided to launch a new themed class each quarter.
subevent.location: Kunming City - Jingxin Yoga Life Center

name: Registered for the 5 km health run at the Kunming Plateau Half Marathon and started training.
description: On September 25, encouraged by He Lu, Sun Yuwei signed up for the 5 km health run affiliated with the Kunming Plateau Half Marathon and began targeted endurance training, moving her training sessions to the banks of the Panlong River. Afterward, she kept running 2 to 3 times a week to prepare for the November event.

subevent.name: Registered for the marathon online and asked about training plans.
subevent.description: Encouraged by her best friend He Lu, Sun Yuwei successfully registered for the 5 km health run in the Kunming Marathon via the official mini program on her phone, and discussed and drew up a preliminary training plan with He Lu on WeChat, agreeing to run together by the Panlong River every week. The two also exchanged details such as running shoe selection and pace goals.

subevent.name: First running training session along the Panlong River
subevent.description: Following her training plan, Sun Yuwei went to the Panlong River in Kunming for her first running session. Wearing her new running shoes, she jogged 3 kilometers along the river to adapt to the pace, recording time, heart rate, and route with her watch, and rehydrating at a rest stop along the way. He Lu was unable to accompany her because of work, but encouraged her via WeChat.

subevent.name: Start running training and gradually improve
subevent.description: Sun Yuwei ran her first 3 km morning run by the Panlong River on the morning of September 28; on the evening of September 29, she went on a 4 km night run with her yoga partner He Lu, exchanging tips on pacing; on the morning of October 1, she ran again in the morning, increasing the distance to 4.5 km, and recorded her reflections. The training covered morning and evening runs, gradually increasing the distance, and she stretched and relaxed after every run.

subevent.name: First solo morning run training.
subevent.description: Sun Yuwei got up at 6 AM on September 27, changed into her running gear, and went to the bank of the Panlong River for her first running training. She started from the starting point, ran 3 kilometers at a comfortable pace, and enjoyed the morning river breeze and scenery along the way. After the run, she did 10 minutes of static stretching at home and recorded the day’s running data.

subevent.name: Night training run with He Lu
subevent.description: On the evening of September 29, Sun Yuwei and her yoga partner He Lu arranged to do their second running training by the Panlong River. They paced each other and completed 4 kilometers together. Along the way, He Lu gave Sun Yuwei advice on adjusting her breathing and rhythm. After the run, they rested and chatted on a riverside bench, then went home separately to stretch and relax.

subevent.name: Advanced solo morning run training.
subevent.description: On the morning of National Day, October 1, Sun Yuwei went alone to the banks of the Panlong River for her third running training session. She tried morning running and gradually increased the distance to 4.5 kilometers, experiencing the tranquility of the holiday morning and the river view. After the run, she did a complete stretching routine by the river and took photos to record her progress. After returning home, she wrote about her running experience in her journal.

subevent.name: Pre-competition preparation and gear organization.
subevent.description: The day before the race, Sun Yuwei organized her race gear at home: washed her running shoes, prepared quick-dry sportswear, pinned her race bib to her T-shirt, filled her water bottle, and packed energy gels. She confirmed the next day's meeting time and place (the marathon starting area) with He Lu on WeChat, and they discussed the locations of aid stations along the course. In the evening, she went to bed early to ensure sufficient sleep.

name: Attend a writing group every Saturday night and connect with the local creative community.
description: After that, Sun Yuwei attended the group activities almost every Saturday evening, gradually getting to know the members and starting to share her creative progress in the group chat. Her essay 'The Shadow of Lake and Mountain' was highly praised in the group, and several members became her loyal readers.

subevent.name: Attend the writing group for the first time and get to know the members.
subevent.description: Starting on the evening of Saturday, September 27, 2025, Sun Yuwei began attending the offline events of the local writing group, held in the activity area on the second floor of Mingyuan Bookstore in Kunming. In the first event, she introduced herself, shared her essay outline, and joined the group's WeChat chat. In the third event, she took part in a peer review of works and privately exchanged writing techniques with member Lin Lu. In the fourth event, she actively shared her experience breaking through creative bottlenecks, added members such as Li Meng as friends, and continued talking in depth at a café after the event. Through participating in these key events, she initially integrated into the local writing community, established personal connections with two or three members, and learned the group's rules and atmosphere.
subevent.location: Kunming City - Mingyuan Bookstore, second-floor activity area.

subevent.name: First time participating in a writing group activity
subevent.description: On the evening of Saturday, September 27, 2025, Sun Yuwei went for the first time to the activity area on the second floor of Mingyuan Bookstore in Kunming to attend the offline gathering of the local writing group. She arrived early and was guided to a seat by Uncle Qin, the bookstore owner. When the activity began, the group leader — a freelance writer in his thirties — organized self-introductions among the new members. Sun Yuwei briefly introduced herself as a Chinese literature major and freelance writer, and shared the outline of the essay she had been working on, about her memories of old Kunming neighborhoods. She then listened carefully to the other members' creative sharing. After the event, she took the initiative to add the group leader on WeChat and joined the group's WeChat chat. The whole process lasted about two hours, and she felt the community atmosphere was friendly and professional.
subevent.location: Kunming City - Mingyuan Bookstore, second-floor activity area.

subevent.name: Attending the writing group activity for the third time.
subevent.description: On the evening of Saturday, October 11, 2025, Sun Yuwei attended the third writing group activity, still held in the activity area on the second floor of Mingyuan Bookstore. This session was a peer review segment. Sun Yuwei had printed out a new prose excerpt (about 1,500 words) in advance and asked the group members for feedback. The group leader and the other two members—Lin Lu, a female member skilled in poetry, and Zhang Fan, a male member writing nonfiction—gave pertinent revision suggestions. Sun Yuwei carefully recorded the suggestions and, after the activity, took the initiative to chat with Lin Lu about poetic techniques in prose language. This activity made her feel that she had become part of this small group and began to look forward to the weekly gatherings.
subevent.location: Kunming City - Mingyuan Bookstore, second-floor activity area.

subevent.name: Attended the writing group activity for the fourth time and deepened connections
subevent.description: On the evening of Saturday, October 18, 2025, Sun Yuwei attended the fourth writing group activity. The theme of this event was "Creative Bottlenecks and Breakthroughs," and each member shared their experience overcoming difficulties. Sun Yuwei spoke actively and honestly admitted that she sometimes procrastinates due to perfectionism. The group leader and several members encouraged her. Among them, Li Meng (a freelance illustrator), a writer of the same age, proactively added her on WeChat and said she would also like to do journaling and writing together. After the activity, Sun Yuwei continued chatting with Li Meng and Chen Chen at a nearby café, exchanged more writing insights, and agreed to interact more often in the group chat. Through four weeks of participation, she had initially integrated into this local creative community, formed personal friendships with two or three members, and gained a full understanding of the group's rules and atmosphere.
subevent.location: Kunming City - Mingyuan Bookstore, second-floor activity area.

subevent.name: Deeply engage in the event and share my creative progress.
subevent.description: Over the following month or so (October 26 to November 29), Sun Yuwei participated more actively in the writing group's activities. She began regularly sharing her creative progress in the group chat, including prose pieces she was revising and the writing bottlenecks she encountered. At the Saturday evening sessions, she took turns reading her work aloud and received feedback from group members. She gradually built deeper trusting relationships with several members, and they started recommending books and writing resources to one another. She also took the initiative to help the group leader compile the minutes of each session and handled some simple community maintenance tasks, further consolidating her presence in the group. During this phase, she agreed with a group member who also loved prose to exchange manuscripts privately, forming a mutual writing-support relationship.
subevent.location: Kunming City - Mingyuan Bookstore, second-floor activity area.

subevent.name: Begin sharing creative progress and bottlenecks
subevent.description: In the writing group chat, Sun Yuwei took the initiative to share the essay excerpt she was revising and the writing bottlenecks she had encountered, such as paragraphs not flowing smoothly and emotional expression not being delicate enough. She posted a long message describing her confusion in detail and invited other group members to offer suggestions. Several members responded quickly; group leader Chen Ming gave encouragement, and member Zhao Xue shared a similar experience of her own. This sharing marked the beginning of Sun Yuwei's deeper integration into the group.
subevent.location: Kunming - Mingyuan Bookstore Second-Floor Activity Area (online group chat)

subevent.name: Attend the first Saturday evening reading and feedback session
subevent.description: At eight in the evening, Sun Yuwei attended the weekly Saturday evening writing group activity in the activity area on the second floor of Mingyuan Book House. She volunteered to read aloud an essay she had recently revised about the old streets of Kunming; it lasted about five minutes. After the reading, the group members gave feedback in turn, including suggestions on structure, word choice refinement, and ways to strengthen the emotion. Sun Yuwei carefully noted down and responded to everyone's opinions, and felt the warmth and support of the group.
subevent.location: Kunming City - Mingyuan Bookstore, second-floor activity area.

subevent.name: Arranged with Zhao Xue to exchange manuscripts privately.
subevent.description: After the first Saturday evening event, Sun Yuwei and Zhao Xue, a group member who also loved essays, had an in-depth exchange via WeChat. The two discovered that their aesthetics and writing styles for essays were highly compatible, and agreed to exchange several of their most satisfying manuscripts within the next two weeks for one-on-one detailed feedback. They also drew up a specific exchange schedule and feedback methods, forming a mutual-aid writing relationship.

subevent.name: Attended the second Saturday evening event and began organizing the minutes
subevent.description: The second Saturday evening activity was held in the activity area on the second floor of Mingyuan Bookstore. Sun Yuwei brought a notebook and took the initiative to record the key discussion points during the activity. After it ended, she sent the organized minutes to the group chat, earning gratitude from group leader Chen Ming and likes from the other members. During the activity, she also read aloud the opening of another newly written essay and continued to receive feedback. Afterward, she and several group members began recommending books and writing resources to one another.
subevent.location: Kunming City - Mingyuan Bookstore, second-floor activity area.

subevent.name: Attending the third Saturday evening event and deepening connections
subevent.description: The third Saturday evening activity was held as scheduled in the activity area on the second floor of Mingyuan Book House. This time, Sun Yuwei read the work she had revised after exchanging manuscripts with Zhao Xue, showing the results of their collaborative writing. During the activity, she proactively recommended several essay collections she had recently read and online writing course resources to the group members, and also accepted recommendations from other members. After the activity, she further discussed community management methods with the group leader, Chen Ming, and volunteered to help with check-in and host the warm-up session at the next activity.
subevent.location: Kunming City - Mingyuan Bookstore, second-floor activity area.

subevent.name: Attend the fourth Saturday evening event and consolidate my role in the community.
subevent.description: The fourth Saturday evening activity was held in the activity area on the second floor of Mingyuan Book House, and it was also the last group activity of this phase. Sun Yuwei arrived early to help the group leader Chen Ming set up the venue, and she gave a short opening speech when the activity began. She read aloud a complete essay that she had revised during four weeks of deep participation, and received warm applause from the whole group. name: Making yoga and meditation a daily practice has significantly improved her physical and mental health
description: Starting in November, Sun Yuwei fully integrated yoga and meditation into her daily life, doing 15 minutes of breathing meditation and posture stretching at 6 a.m. every day. After a month of consistent practice, she felt that the stiffness in her shoulders and neck had improved significantly, her anxiety had lessened, and her sleep quality had improved. Inspiration emerged during practice, and she wrote ten short poems based on her introspection experiences, collected as 'Meditation Notes' and published on the Xiaohongshu account 'Yuwei Slow Record' on November 25, where it resonated with readers.

subevent.name: Phase 1: Establish a daily yoga and meditation habit
subevent.description: On November 1, 2025, Sun Yuwei started a daily yoga and meditation plan. Every morning at 6 a.m., she did 15 minutes of breathing meditation and posture stretching in her bedroom at home in Wuhua District, Kunming. After ten consecutive days of practice, she had initially established a regular habit, felt her body gradually relax and her mind become calm, and the stiffness in her shoulders and neck had eased.

subevent.name: First day of yoga meditation practice
subevent.description: At 6 a.m., Sun Yuwei began Day 1 of practice on her yoga mat in her bedroom at home in Wuhua District, Kunming. She first did five minutes of breathing meditation, focusing on diaphragmatic breathing, followed by ten minutes of basic pose stretches, including Cat-Cow, Downward-Facing Dog, and Child's Pose. After finishing, she recorded her feelings: her body felt slightly stretched and relaxed.

subevent.name: Next day yoga and meditation practice
subevent.description: At 6 a.m., Sun Yuwei continued her second day of practice in the bedroom. She repeated breathing meditation and posture stretching, trying to make the movements more fluid. After finishing, she felt warmth in the shoulder and neck area and was relatively calm.

subevent.name: Day 3 yoga and meditation practice
subevent.description: At 6 a.m., Sun Yuwei did her Day 3 practice in the bedroom. The number of times her attention wandered during breathing meditation decreased, and she deliberately deepened the range of motion in the posture stretches. After finishing, she felt that her body's flexibility had improved slightly.

subevent.name: Day four of yoga and meditation practice
subevent.description: At 6 a.m., Sun Yuwei began Day 4 of practice right on time. The breathing meditation lasted 5 minutes, and Warrior I and Triangle pose were added to the asana stretches. The movements went smoothly, and she felt clear and refreshed after practice.

subevent.name: Fifth day yoga and meditation practice.
subevent.description: At 6 a.m., Day 5 of practice. Sun Yuwei tried to focus on the space between her eyebrows during breathing meditation while keeping the stretching poses unchanged. After finishing, she noted that her shoulder and neck stiffness had eased noticeably and she felt calm inside.

subevent.name: Day 6 yoga and meditation practice.
subevent.description: At 6 a.m., Sun Yuwei did her sixth day of practice. During breathing meditation she added counting breaths, while the asana stretching sequence remained the same. After practice, she felt her breathing was deeper and longer and her body felt light and relaxed.

subevent.name: Day 7 yoga and meditation practice
subevent.description: At 6 a.m., Day 7 of practice. After breathing meditation, Sun Yuwei tried a fusion asana flow, transitioning smoothly from Cat-Cow into Downward-Facing Dog. After the practice she was lightly sweating, and her timing was well managed.

subevent.name: Day 8 Yoga and Meditation Practice
subevent.description: At 6 a.m., Sun Yuwei started her eighth day of practice. Breathing meditation remained steady, and she tried adding the Wind-Blown Tree Pose to her posture stretching. After finishing, she felt relaxed all over and in a good mood.

subevent.name: Day 9 yoga and meditation practice
subevent.description: At 6 a.m., Day 9 of practice. After breathing meditation, Sun Yuwei focused on the precision of her asanas and adjusted the arm position in Downward-Facing Dog. After practice, she felt her shoulders and neck completely relaxed, and her confidence in building the habit grew.

subevent.name: Day 10 of yoga meditation practice
subevent.description: At 6:00 a.m., on the last day of practice, Sun Yuwei completed the breathing meditation and prescribed postures in full, and added an extra 2 minutes of rest. After finishing, she recorded her experience over ten consecutive days, summarized the improvement in her physical condition, and initially established a regular morning routine.

subevent.name: Phase 2: Deepening insight and recording inspiration.
subevent.description: Sun Yuwei continued her daily 6 a.m. yoga and meditation practice for 9 days. During this phase, she focused more on inner observation, using her phone or journal to jot down fragments of inspiration that emerged between meditation sessions, accumulating material for future creative work. After practice, she clearly felt less anxiety and improved sleep quality.

subevent.name: Day 1: Morning Yoga, Meditation, and Inspiration Notes
subevent.description: At 6 a.m. on November 11, 2025, Sun Yuwei began her yoga and meditation practice on time in her bedroom at her home in Kunming. She first did 5 minutes of breath regulation, then completed 15 minutes of basic yoga postures (such as cat-cow and downward-facing dog) to stretch her body, and then sat cross-legged in meditation for 30 minutes. During a break in the meditation, she took out the journal she carried with her and wrote down the fragments of inspiration that surfaced, including a prose draft about autumn street scenes and a reflection on personal growth. After the practice, she felt relaxed in body and mind, and her introspective experience deepened.

subevent.name: Day 2 morning yoga meditation and inspiration record
subevent.description: At 6 a.m. on November 12, 2025, Sun Yuwei continued her yoga and meditation practice in her bedroom at home in Kunming. She then sat quietly in meditation for 25 minutes. During the meditation, she quickly used the memo app on her phone to jot down observation notes about the atmosphere of Kunming's old streets and a warm snippet of conversation with her mother. After the practice, she felt her anxiety further reduced and her mind clearer.

subevent.name: Day 3 morning yoga, meditation, and inspiration recording
subevent.description: At 6 a.m. on November 13, 2025, Sun Yuwei began a new day of yoga and meditation in her bedroom at home in Kunming. During a break in the meditation, she used her journal to write down a poetic metaphor about the changing seasons and an opening sentence for a future essay. After practice, she felt increased body flexibility and improved sleep quality.

subevent.name: Day 4: morning yoga, meditation, and inspiration notes.

After the practice, she felt calmer inside and her creative inspiration became clearer.

During a break in the meditation, she used her journal to write down a prose outline about the rainy season in Kunming, as well as an insight inspired by a book recommended by her advisor Wu Mingyuan. After the practice, she felt her anxiety had significantly subsided and creative inspiration flowed without end.

subevent.name: Day 6: Morning Yoga, Meditation, and Inspiration Notes
subevent.description: At 6 a.m. on November 16, 2025, Sun Yuwei practiced yoga and meditation in her bedroom at home in Kunming. She first spent 5 minutes in simple meditation to calm her mind, then did 20 minutes of therapeutic yoga poses (such as eagle pose and bridge pose) to relieve her shoulders, neck, and spine, followed by 25 minutes of seated meditation. During a meditation break, she used the memo app on her phone to record a memory about details of her father Sun Mingyuan's work and an essay topic about a family dinner. After the practice, she felt light in her body and more confident in her writing.

After the practice, she felt that her sleep quality had significantly improved and her anxiety had almost disappeared.

subevent.name: Day 8: morning yoga, meditation, and inspiration recording
subevent.description: At 6 a.m. on November 18, 2025, Sun Yuwei did yoga and meditation in her bedroom at home in Kunming. She first relaxed with 5 minutes of abdominal breathing, then completed a 20-minute vinyasa flow sequence (such as camel pose and fish pose) to open the chest and heart chakra, followed by 25 minutes of seated meditation. During a break in the meditation, she used the notes app on her phone to record a vivid description of the autumn scenery at Green Lake Park in Kunming, as well as a story idea that came from communicating with her editor Xu Mingyuan. After the practice, she felt energized and highly creative.

subevent.name: Day 9: Morning yoga, meditation, and recording inspiration
subevent.description: At 6 a.m. on November 19, 2025, Sun Yuwei did yoga and meditation in her bedroom at home in Kunming. She started with 10 minutes of stretching, then completed 15 minutes of Hatha yoga poses (such as headstand preparation and shoulderstand) to strengthen her core and blood circulation, followed by 30 minutes of meditation. During a break in the meditation, she used her journal to write down a story idea about her college roommate Liu Jia's future development in Chengdu, as well as a memorable quote about inner freedom. After the practice, she felt body and mind unified, and her introspective experience reached a new depth.

subevent.name: Phase 3: Practice consistently and complete the creative work.
subevent.description: Sun Yuwei continued her daily morning yoga and meditation practice. During this period (November 21 to November 30), she turned her introspective experiences into ten short poems, compiled as Meditation Notes. On November 25, she published the complete poems on her Xiaohongshu account "Yuwei Slow Record." Reviewing at the end of the month, she felt a significant improvement in her physical and mental health; neck and shoulder stiffness, anxiety, and sleep problems had all greatly improved.

subevent.name: Daily morning yoga and meditation practice
subevent.description: Sun Yuwei gets up at 6:30 every morning and does about 40 minutes of yoga and meditation practice in her bedroom at home. Specifically: 10 minutes of warm-up stretching, 20 minutes of yoga poses (such as Cat-Cow, Downward-Facing Dog, and the Warrior series) to relieve stiffness in her shoulders and neck, followed by 10 minutes of seated meditation focusing on breath and introspection. She plays soft meditation music during the practice and uses a mobile app to record the duration and feelings after finishing. She kept up this practice every day without fail from November 21 to November 30.

subevent.name: Transform the introspection experience into ten short poems and compile them into 'Meditation Notes'.
subevent.description: After several consecutive days of yoga and meditation, Sun Yuwei accumulated rich introspective experience. On November 24, all day long, at the desk in her bedroom at home, she distilled the images and insights that surfaced during meditation into ten short poems, each four to eight lines, with themes covering breath, bodily sensations, emotional flow, and natural imagery. Afterwards she transcribed the poems into her journal with a fountain pen and designed a simple cover, gathering them into a collection titled Meditation Notes. During this time she repeatedly refined the wording until she was satisfied in the evening.

subevent.name: Published "Meditation Notes" on Xiaohongshu.
subevent.description: On the morning of November 25, Sun Yuwei logged into Xiaohongshu using her alternate account 'Yuwei Slow Record' and published all ten short poems from 'Meditation Notes' as image-and-text posts. She first used her camera to photograph the poetry pages in her journal, then used a photo-editing app to add soft filters and text titles, accompanied by a note of about 200 characters explaining the creative motivation, mentioning that this was the result of a week of consistent yoga and meditation. After publishing, she replied to several comments and shared the posts to her WeChat Moments and the writer's group.

subevent.name: At the end of the month, review physical and mental changes
subevent.description: On the evening of November 30, after finishing her final yoga meditation, Sun Yuwei sat by the window and reviewed her practice and writing from the latter part of November. She looked through the daily meditation notes and the manuscript of Meditation Notes in her journal and felt that the stiffness in her shoulders and neck had clearly eased, her time to fall asleep had shortened from 45 minutes to 15 minutes, and her daytime anxiety attacks had dropped from two or three times a day to almost zero. She wrote a summary in her phone memo and planned to maintain this habit in the long term. Then she shared the joy of this change with her mother, Li Xiulan.

subevent.name: Published 'Meditation Notes' on Xiaohongshu.
subevent.description: On November 25, 2025, Sun Yuwei compiled ten short poems she had written during the past month of yoga and meditation practice into a collection titled "Meditation Notes," and edited and published it on her Xiaohongshu account "Yuwei's Slow Notes" via her phone. She also included practice reflections and hand-drawn illustrations. After posting, it received much resonance and interaction from readers.
